result.summary:
The `Zeta23/PairCeiling/` directory (11 files, ~2000 lines, sorry-free, standard axioms only) formalizes the paper's optimality remark for Theorem B: a CEILING on what any "bandwidth-one certificate" can certify about the proportion of simple critical-line zeros. The formal objects are: a grid configuration = a "form factor" S : ℕ → ℝ at integer frequencies j = 1..N, inducing atom masses s_j := S(j)/N at grid points j/N ∈ (0,1]; the cumulative step C(x) = Σ_{j/N ≤ x} s_j; the discrepancy D := C − x²/2 against the GUE datum k dk; and the integrated discrepancy E := ∫₀ˣ D (Defs.lean). A certificate is an (anonymous) tuple (c₀, r) with r ∈ C¹[0,1] (HasDerivAt r g on Icc 0 1, g continuous on [0,1]), g differentiable off a countable set T with derivative h interval-integrable on [0,1]; its VALUE is v := c₀ + ∫₀¹ r(x)·x dx (pairing with the GUE density on the closed band [0,1] only — this is where "bandwidth one" lives), and it is VALID at a configuration with simple-point fraction p iff c₀ + Σ_{j=1}^N s_j r(j/N) ≤ p. The analytic core (Stability.lean) is two exact integration-by-parts/Abel identities — Σ_j s_j r(j/N) − ∫₀¹ r(x)x dx = r(1)D(1) − ∫₀¹ g·D = r(1)D(1) − g(1)E(1) + ∫₀¹ h·E — and the resulting `ceiling_stability`: |Σ_j s_j r(j/N) − ∫₀¹ r(x)x dx| ≤ |r(1)|·|D(1)| + |g(1)|·|E(1)| + M·∫₀¹|h| whenever |E| ≤ M on [0,1], with NO sign condition on s. Ceiling.lean converts this to: validity at ONE configuration ⇒ v ≤ p + |r(1)|·|D(1)| + |r′(1)|·|E(1)| + (sup|E|)·∫₀¹|r″|.

NearCUE.lean specializes to laws whose open-band rows match the sine-process/CUE value: NearCUE S N τ := ∀ 1 ≤ j < N, |N·S(j) − j| ≤ τ (row j = N, the closed-band edge, is FREE). By an exact cellwise computation (N³E(x) = (−m + 3mθ(1−θ) − θ³)/6 + perturbation, with −(m+1) ≤ cubic ≤ 0) it proves sup_{[0,1]}|E| ≤ 1/(6N²) + τ/(2N), giving `ceiling_nearCUE`: v ≤ p + d₁|r(1)| + (1/(6N²) + τ/(2N))(|r′(1)| + ∫₀¹|r″|) for any valid certificate, where |D(1)| ≤ d₁. RowCert.lean/NumericCert.lean provide pure-integer certificate checkers (`checkRows`, `check`) with soundness theorems: from kernel-checkable integer enclosures lo_j ≤ K·S(j) ≤ hi_j they derive NearCUE and |D(1)| bounds for EVERY real S inside the enclosures. LawN256.lean instantiates: an explicit 256-periodic law with K = 2^140, 256 width-one integer enclosures (rows 1..255 pinned to j·K/256 within one ulp; row 256 free, S(256) ≈ 211.43, i.e. an edge atom of mass ≈ 0.826 at frequency 1), τ = 3·10⁻⁴⁰, d₁ = 0.82395317. The law itself is S(j) = (Σ_c w_c |Σ_i m_{c,i} e^{2πi j x_{c,i}/256}|²)/256 over marked configurations — rational weights w_c ≥ 0 summing to 1, rational positions x_{c,i} ∈ [0,256), marks m_{c,i} ∈ {1,2} with Σ_i m_{c,i} = 256 — the optimal solution of an exact-rational LINEAR PROGRAMME over 256-periodic marked configurations, recorded in cert_N256_blk_b128m.json (sha256 cc3de9917db4d14d844630a4e97dda8387fd6e257e52b6967f430b8914584eb8, held by the authors, NOT in the repo). Its simple-point fraction is exactly p₀ = 10909258999421303588095230195816054408197/16000000000000000000000000000000000000000 = 0.68182868746…. `LawN256_check : checkRows LawN256 = true` and `LawN256_edge : edgeNonneg LawN256 = true` are proved by `decide +kernel` (axiom audit: [propext] and none, respectively). CeilingLaw256.lean/Signed.lean give the final caps: for every S with EnclOK and every valid certificate, v ≤ p + 0.82395317·|r(1)| + 2.5431316·10⁻⁶·(|r′(1)| + ∫₀¹|r″|) (`ceiling_law256_decimal`), and — since D(1) ≥ 0 is kernel-checked — for certificates with r(1) ≥ 0 the edge term is dropped entirely: v ≤ p + 2.5431316·10⁻⁶·(|r′(1)| + ∫₀¹|r″|) (`ceiling_law256_signed`). With p = p₀ this is the headline: every bandwidth-one certificate certifies a simple-zero proportion at most 0.6818287 + 2.55·10⁻⁶·(|r′(1)| + ∫|r″|). For calibration: the paper's Theorem B achieves 2/3 = 0.6667 and Theorem D (optimal Montgomery–Taylor window) achieves 2 − 1/c₁* = 0.67250; the residual headroom inside the certificate format is thus ≈ 0.0093.

Logical form, precisely (from `ceiling_law256_signed`, Signed.lean:94): FOR ALL S : ℕ → ℝ with EnclOK LawN256.K S 0 LawN256.encl [class Y — every real form factor inside the 256 kernel-recorded integer enclosures; the actual LP law is one member, by external interval arithmetic]; FOR ALL (c₀, r, g, h, T, p) with (i) ∀ x ∈ Icc 0 1, HasDerivAt r (g x) x, (ii) ContinuousOn g (Icc 0 1), (iii) T countable and ∀ x ∈ Ioo 0 1 \ T, HasDerivAt g (h x) x, (iv) IntervalIntegrable h volume 0 1, (v) 0 ≤ r 1, (vi) c₀ + Σ_{j=1}^{256} (S j/256)·r(j/256) ≤ p [type X — a bandwidth-one certificate valid at the configuration]: THEN c₀ + ∫₀¹ r(x)·x dx ≤ p + 2.5431316e-6·|g 1| + 2.5431316e-6·∫₀¹|h| [cap Z]. The bridge from the paper's Theorem B machinery to hypothesis (vi) — that a paper certificate, being valid against every admissible zero-configuration, is in particular valid configuration-by-configuration at the law's support and hence, averaged over w_c, at the law with p = p₀ — is a paper-level remark, not formalized (PairCeiling has no comparator trusted-statement file; AUDIT.md documents this).

key_items.name: Configuration data (Csum, Cstep, Dfun, Efun)
key_items.statement: For weights s : ℕ → ℝ at grid points j/N: Csum s m = Σ_{j=1}^m s j; Cstep s N x = Σ_{1≤j≤N, j/N≤x} s j (right-continuous); Dfun := Cstep − x²/2 (discrepancy vs the GUE datum k dk); Efun := ∫₀ˣ Dfun. massOf S N j := S j / N converts a form factor S to atom masses (Bridge.lean:31).

key_items.name: abel_ibp_first / abel_ibp_second (exact identities)
key_items.statement: (1) Σ_{j=1}^N s_j r(j/N) − ∫₀¹ r(x)x dx = r(1)·D(1) − ∫₀¹ g·D, for r with HasDerivAt r (g x) on Icc 0 1, g continuous on [0,1]. (2) If additionally g is differentiable off a countable T with derivative h, h interval-integrable: = r(1)·D(1) − g(1)·E(1) + ∫₀¹ h·E. Proved by cellwise FTC + Abel summation + FTC off a countable set. No sign condition on s.

key_items.name: ceiling_stability (THE stability inequality)
key_items.statement: Hypotheses: 0 < N; T ⊆ ℝ countable; ∀ x ∈ Icc 0 1, HasDerivAt r (g x) x; ContinuousOn g (Icc 0 1); ∀ x ∈ Ioo 0 1 \ T, HasDerivAt g (h x) x; IntervalIntegrable h volume 0 1; ∀ x ∈ Icc 0 1, |Efun s N x| ≤ M. Conclusion: |Σ_{j=1}^N s_j r(j/N) − ∫₀¹ r(x)x dx| ≤ |r 1|·|Dfun s N 1| + |g 1|·|Efun s N 1| + M·∫₀¹|h|. No sign/positivity condition on s whatsoever.

key_items.name: ceiling_of_valid_at / ceiling_numeric (certificate language)
key_items.statement: If additionally c₀ + Σ_j s_j r(j/N) ≤ p₁ (validity at ONE configuration), then the value v := c₀ + ∫₀¹ r(x)·x dx obeys v ≤ p₁ + |r 1|·|D 1| + |g 1|·|E 1| + M·∫₀¹|h|; parametrised: with |D(1)| ≤ d₁, |E(1)| ≤ e₁, sup|E| ≤ M, |r(1)| ≤ a, |r′(1)| ≤ b, ∫|r″| ≤ c: v ≤ p₁ + d₁a + e₁b + Mc.

key_items.name: NearCUE and the E-bound
key_items.statement: NearCUE S N τ := ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → j < N → |N·S(j) − j| ≤ τ (row j = N free). Theorem abs_Efun_le_of_nearCUE: for 0 ≤ τ and NearCUE S N τ, ∀ x ∈ [0,1], |Efun (massOf S N) N x| ≤ 1/(6N²) + τ/(2N). Proof is the exact cell identity N³E(x) = (−m + 3mθ(1−θ) − θ³)/6 + P + Δθ with |P| ≤ m(m−1)τ/2, |Δ| ≤ mτ and −(m+1) ≤ −m+3mθ(1−θ)−θ³ ≤ 0.

key_items.name: ceiling_nearCUE
key_items.statement: For any grid form factor S with NearCUE S N τ and |Dfun (massOf S N) N 1| ≤ d₁, and any certificate (c₀,r,g,h,T) as in ceiling_stability with validity c₀ + Σ_{j=1}^N (S j/N)·r(j/N) ≤ p: c₀ + ∫₀¹ r(x)x dx ≤ p + d₁·|r 1| + (1/(6N²)+τ/(2N))·|g 1| + (1/(6N²)+τ/(2N))·∫₀¹|h|.

key_items.name: EnclOK (the ONE displayed hypothesis)
key_items.statement: EnclOK K S j l : Prop — the list l = [(lo,hi),…] satisfies lo ≤ K·S(j+1) ≤ hi, recursively in order. For LawN256 this is the ONLY unproved-in-Lean input: that the true form factor of the LP law lies in the 256 recorded integer enclosures (established outside Lean by 70-digit interval arithmetic from the exact-rational certificate file).

key_items.name: RowCertData / checkRows / cert_of_checkRows (integer certificate format)
key_items.statement: RowCertData = (N, K, encl : List (ℤ×ℤ), τ = tn/td, d₁ = dn/dd). checkRows runs pure integer arithmetic: each row j < N satisfies |N·lo_j − jK|·td ≤ tn·K and same for hi; and |2·Σlo − KN|·dd ≤ dn·2KN, same for Σhi. Soundness: checkRows d = true → ∀ S with EnclOK d.K S 0 d.encl: NearCUE S d.N (tn/td) ∧ |D(1)| ≤ dn/dd.

key_items.name: LawN256 (the 256-periodic near-CUE law)
key_items.statement: N = 256, K = 2^140 = 1393796574908163946345982392040522594123776; 256 enclosures each of width one ulp: rows 1..255 pinned to j·K/256 (so N·S(j) = j to within 3·10⁻⁴⁰); row 256 free with K·S(256) ≈ 2.9469e44, i.e. S(256) ≈ 211.43, an edge atom of mass s_256 = S(256)/256 ≈ 0.826 at frequency 1; tn/td = 3/10⁴⁰; dn/dd = 82395317/10⁸. Law is S(j) = (Σ_c w_c |Σ_i m_{c,i} e^{2πi j x_{c,i}/256}|²)/256, w_c ≥ 0 rational summing to 1, x_{c,i} ∈ [0,256) rational, marks m_{c,i} ∈ {1,2}, Σ_i m_{c,i} = 256; the optimum of an exact-rational LP over 256-periodic marked configurations; simple-point fraction exactly p₀ = 10909258999421303588095230195816054408197/16000000000000000000000000000000000000000 = 0.68182868746…; certificate file cert_N256_blk_b128m.json, sha256 cc3de9917db4d14d844630a4e97dda8387fd6e257e52b6967f430b8914584eb8 (not in repo).

key_items.name: LawN256_check and LawN256_edge (kernel checks)
key_items.statement: checkRows LawN256 = true and edgeNonneg LawN256 = true, both by `decide +kernel` — no native_decide; axiom audit: LawN256_check depends only on [propext], LawN256_edge on no axioms. These give, for every S in the enclosures: NearCUE S 256 (3/10⁴⁰), |D(1)| ≤ 0.82395317, and D(1) ≥ 0 (edgeNonneg checks K·N ≤ 2·Σlo, i.e. T_N/N ≥ 1/2).

key_items.name: ceiling_signed / ceiling_law256_signed (the headline cap)
key_items.statement: When r(1) ≥ 0 and D(1) ≥ 0 the edge term −r(1)·D(1) of the second identity is ≤ 0 and DROPPED: c₀ + ∫₀¹ r(x)x dx ≤ p + 2.5431316e-6·|g 1| + 2.5431316e-6·∫₀¹|h| for every valid certificate with r(1) ≥ 0, for every S in the LawN256 enclosures. With p = p₀ = 0.68182868746… this is the paper's cap: every bandwidth-one certificate certifies at most 0.6818287 + 2.55·10⁻⁶·(|r′(1)| + ∫₀¹|r″|). Compare achieved values: Thm B = 2/3, Thm D = 2 − 1/c₁* = 0.67250 — headroom ≈ 0.0093.

key_items.name: Alternative full-grid certificate route (unused by LawN256)
key_items.statement: NumericCert.lean's CertData/check/cert_of_check propagate integer interval bounds for K·T_j, K·U_j through one loop and certify four families: |D(1)| ≤ bD1, |E(1)| ≤ bE1, sup grid |Dleft/Dright| ≤ b1, max_j|Egrid j| + sup|D|/N ≤ b2; Bridge.lean's package_of_check turns these into the four interval hypotheses of ceiling_numeric (using: D decreases between atoms; |Efun(x) − Egrid(m)| ≤ sup|D|/N). This handles laws that are NOT near-CUE; LawN256 instead uses the cheaper RowCert route.

key_items.name: Where bandwidth-one lives in the parent method
key_items.statement: PrimeSideA's Setting carries the 'bandwidth ratio' λ with 0 < λ ≤ 1, mollifier/Dirichlet-polynomial length X = (T/2π)^λ, L = λ·log(T/2π); the cap λ ≤ 1 (Montgomery–Vaughan regime, unconditional mean values) is exactly what restricts the method's pairing to the form factor on the closed band [0,1]; several lemmas are proved 'without the bandwidth cap' with absorbing hypothesis L ≤ B, marking where λ ≤ 1 is genuinely used.

result.bandwidth_role: Bandwidth-one enters in three coordinated places. (1) In the certificate's VALUE functional v = c₀ + ∫₀¹ r(x)·x dx: the weight r is only defined/hypothesized on [0,1] and is paired against the density x dx — the GUE form-factor value on the band |α| ≤ 1, the only region where Montgomery-type unconditional information exists. (2) In the VALIDITY pairing c₀ + Σ_{j=1}^N (S j/N)·r(j/N) ≤ p: the certificate interrogates the configuration's form factor only at frequencies j/N ∈ (0,1] — nothing about S(j) for j > N (frequencies > 1) enters any hypothesis or conclusion, so the adversarial law is completely unconstrained above the band edge, and constrained to within 3·10⁻⁴⁰ of CUE strictly inside it. The closed-band edge j = N is deliberately left free (the LP puts a large atom of mass ≈ 0.826 there), which is what makes p₀ = 0.6818… < 1 achievable while remaining CUE-consistent in the open band. (3) In the parent method (PrimeSideA), the same limitation appears as the mollifier length cap: Setting.lam = λ ∈ (0,1], X = (T/2π)^λ; the Montgomery–Vaughan generalized Hilbert inequality controls mean values only for Dirichlet polynomials of length ≤ T, i.e., λ ≤ 1, and this is precisely why the paper's certificates factor through the band-[0,1] pairing that the ceiling then caps. The ceiling is thus the formal statement: the information content of bandwidth-one pair-correlation data (open-band form factor + edge mass + simple-point fraction, processed linearly) saturates at 0.68182868746….
limitations: The cap binds only the exact certificate format X: a scalar c₀ plus a LINEAR pairing of one weight r against the pair-correlation measure on [0,1], compared to the simple-point fraction. It is an impossibility theorem for this format, not for the analytic problem: approaches not factoring through this pairing (moments of ζ, zero-density, non-linear positivity, Levinson-type with different observables) are formally untouched.

Higher bandwidth is outside scope by construction: no hypothesis constrains S(j) for j > 256 (frequencies > 1), and the value functional stops at 1. A certificate exploiting form-factor information on (1, Δ] (which would require new mean-value theorems for Dirichlet polynomials of length T^Δ, Δ > 1 — the known fundamental obstruction) simply does not satisfy the theorem's shape and is not bounded by it.

Multi-linear / higher-correlation functionals are outside scope: the configuration class Y records ONLY the pair form factor S and the simple fraction p. Certificates pairing with triple correlations, k-level densities, or joint distributions would need a richer adversarial law matching those observables too; nothing here shows the same law (or any law) defeats them.

The numeric cap is NOT uniform over certificates: the bound is p₀ + 2.5431316e-6·(|r′(1)| + ∫₀¹|r″|), degrading linearly in the certificate's second-variation mass; at fixed N = 256 a certificate with ∫|r″| ~ 10⁴ would only be capped near 0.707. Pinning rough certificates requires larger N, but the law (and possibly p₀(N)) must be re-derived by a new LP at that N — the dependence of the LP value on N is not formalized.

Certificates with r(1) < 0 escape the signed cap and only receive the weaker unsigned bound with +0.82395317·|r(1)|; the headline number 0.6818287 requires r(1) ≥ 0 (signed theorem) or r(1) = 0 (decimal instance as stated in the CeilingLaw256 docstring).

Regularity boundary of X: r must be genuinely C¹ on [0,1] (HasDerivAt everywhere on Icc, g continuous); r′ may fail differentiability only on a countable set and r″ must be interval-integrable. Certificates with corner points in r (jump in r′) or distributional components are outside the formal class (though approximable at the cost of ∫|r″| → large).

Trust boundary: EnclOK — that the actual LP law's form factor lies in the 256 recorded enclosures — is a displayed hypothesis verified only by external 70-digit interval arithmetic on a JSON file identified by sha256 and 'available from the authors'; it is not in the repository and not replayable from the artifact alone. Likewise p₀ = 1 − a_N being the law's simple fraction, and the law being the LP OPTIMUM, are paper-side claims (p enters the Lean theorems as a free variable).

One-sidedness: the formalization proves the ceiling (upper bound via one adversarial law) but NOT tightness — no formalized matching certificate/LP-dual showing 0.68182868746 is attained; nor any formalized statement that the paper's Theorem B/D certificates actually satisfy hypothesis (vi) at this law (that bridge is a paper-level remark; PairCeiling has no comparator trusted-statement file).

The adversarial law uses marks in {1,2} only (simple or double points). This suffices for the ceiling (any admissible configuration works as an adversary), but means the ceiling does not quantify what certificates could say about higher multiplicities or about the distinct-zeros functional of Theorem C — those would need separate laws/LPs.
extension_hooks: ceiling_stability (Stability.lean:305) carries NO sign condition on s and is generic in (s, N): it is a general grid-vs-continuum comparison for signed discrete measures against x²/2, reusable verbatim for other spectral statistics (e.g. ξ′ zero statistics in Zeta23/XiPrime/, Dirichlet L-function analogues, or laws matching non-GUE reference densities by swapping the x²/2 datum in Dfun).

The whole RowCert/NumericCert integer-certificate machinery is parametric in (N, K, encl, τ, d₁): plugging in a larger-N law (e.g. N = 4096) shrinks the stability constant 1/(6N²) from 2.54e-6 to ~1e-8 and re-pins rougher certificates; only a new external LP solve + enclosure computation is needed — no new Lean analysis. Tracking the LP value p₀(N) as N → ∞ would identify the true asymptotic bandwidth-one cap (is 0.681828687… already the limit, or does p₀(N) decrease?).

Discharge EnclOK inside Lean: the law is finitely supported with rational data, and S(j) is a finite rational-trigonometric sum; formalizing interval evaluation of cos/sin at rational multiples of 2π/256 (or an algebraic-number computation in a cyclotomic field ℚ(ζ_256), where S(j) is an explicit element) would remove the only displayed hypothesis and make the ceiling fully self-contained. The cyclotomic route is particularly clean: K·S(j) ∈ ℚ(ζ_256) is exactly computable.

Formalize the LP dual: a matching certificate (c₀*, r*) achieving ≈ p₀ at the law would prove the ceiling TIGHT, mirroring lemmaR_tight (ZeroSide/TightMult.lean) which already does this for the rank–trace inequality. That would convert the remark 'the method saturates at 0.68183' into a two-sided theorem and identify exactly which structural feature (the free edge atom) is the binding constraint — the natural target for any attempt to beat it.

Extend the identity chain one order: abel_ibp_first → abel_ibp_second iterates integration by parts; a third-order identity (introduce F := ∫₀ˣ E, bound sup|F| ≤ O(1/N³) for near-CUE laws) would cap certificates assuming only r‴ ∈ L¹, widening the pinned class and improving the roughness dependence from |r′(1)| + ∫|r″| to |r″(1)| + ∫|r‴| with N⁻³ constants.

Enrich the configuration class Y and rebuild the LP: the marked-configuration format (weights w_c, positions x_{c,i}, marks m_{c,i}, |FT|² form factor) extends naturally to record triple correlations or k-level data; an analogous grid law + integer-enclosure certificate would produce the first formal ceiling for multi-linear certificates and quantify exactly how much a 3-level-density upgrade of the method could buy — the most informative next computation for the research program.

Weaken the closed-band edge freedom: the LP's entire advantage lives in the free row j = N (edge atom 0.826, D(1) = 0.824). Any new analytic input constraining the form factor AT frequency 1 (e.g. an asymptotic for the mollified second moment at length exactly T, or a Goldston–Montgomery-type edge regularity statement) would shrink the feasible set; re-running the LP under an added edge constraint measures precisely the value of such a theorem before anyone proves it. The Lean framework accepts this as a modified RowCertData with a constrained final row.

The first_order_bound (Stability.lean:169) gives an alternative error currency (sup|D| instead of sup|E|, paying ∫|r′| instead of ∫|r″|): certificates with small first variation but large second variation are better capped through it; a combined optimization over the two routes is unformalized but immediate.

The general-law route NumericCert/Bridge (check/cert_of_check/package_of_check) certifies arbitrary grid laws, not just near-CUE ones: it enables ceilings at laws that trade open-band CUE-agreement for other features (e.g. laws matching the actual unconditional constraints on F(α) with error terms), probing which constraint set really forces the 0.682 number.

result.summary:
This repository is a sorry-free Lean 4/Mathlib formalization (Lean v4.33.0-rc2, no extra axioms) of "More than two thirds of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie on the critical line" (Theorems A-E), plus two extras crucial for a follow-up program: a machine-checked TIGHTNESS theorem for the core rank-trace certificate, and a "bandwidth-one ceiling" showing the whole method class saturates near 0.6818. The architecture is a strict two-layer design. The abstract layer (Zeta23/Defs.lean) never mentions riemannZeta: a `ZeroConfig` is any set of distinct points in the closed strip 0<=Re rho<=1 with multiplicities m_rho>=1, locally finite in the ordinate, invariant under the reflection rho -> 1 - conj(rho) with equal multiplicities. Statement.lean instantiates it from Mathlib's riemannZeta via analyticOrderAt (`ZetaSeam`), with sanity anchors tying to Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis. All counting functions (N, N_d, N0, N0*, N0^s, N^s) are defined against this; Theorems A/B/C are the epsilon-forms (2/3-eps)N(T,2T) <= N0*(T,2T), (2/3-eps)N <= N0^s (multiplicity-aware), (5/6-eps)N <= N_d, from fixed-lambda constants H(lambda)=2-1/lambda-lambda/3, G(lambda)=3/2-kappa(lambda)/2 with kappa(lambda)=1/lambda+lambda/3, taking sup over lambda<1.

The engine: pick a grid tau_k = T + 2*pi*k/L (k < d ~ LT/2pi) with L = lambda*log(T/2pi), a taper phi supported exactly on [-L/2, L/2], and form the d x d Weil-explicit-formula Gram matrix G_{kl} = sum_rho m_rho phihat(gamma_rho - tau_k) phihat(gamma_rho - tau_l) (transpose, NOT conjugate-transpose - a bilinear, not sesquilinear, Gram; real-symmetric by the rho -> 1-conj(rho) symmetry). G = A + E where A is the window part (zeros with ordinate in I' = (T-sqrt(T), 2T+sqrt(T)]) and E the tail. In hat-units (division by aL^2, a = L^{-1} integral phi^2), each ON-LINE zero contributes a PSD rank-1 ATOM m_rho * u_rho u_rho^T with real vector u_rho of norm^2 <= aL^2 - this norm bound is EXACT-in-the-limit via the Poisson identity sum_{k in Z} phihat(gamma - tau_k)^2 = aL^2 (lem:poisson; "no edge leak"). Each OFF-LINE pair {rho, 1-conj(rho)} contributes a hyperbolic PAIR-BLOCK m*(u u^T + conj(u) conj(u)^T) = 2m*(x x^T - y y^T), a difference of PSD rank-<=1 matrices, hence signature at most (1,1) REGARDLESS of the depth |beta - 1/2|. So A-hat = P + Q with P PSD, rank P <= s1+s2, tr P <= N_on(I'), and n_+(Q) <= p (number of off-line pairs) by Sylvester inertia. The prime side (explicit formula + Chebyshev-Mertens + Montgomery-Vaughan) computes the two moments: tr G-hat >= (1-delta)N and ||G-hat||_F^2 <= (kappa(lambda)+delta)N. The linear-algebra certificate then converts (moments) + (block structure) + (tail bound, via Weyl with threshold theta_0 ~ X^{1/2} log(4T)/T) into the zero counts.

The heart is "Lemma R" (Zeta23/ZeroSide/RankTraceMult.lean), the multiplicity-aware rank-trace inequality: for P = sum_j m_j v_j v_j^*, Q Hermitian with n_+(Q) <= b, c > 0: 2c*tr(P+Q) - ||P+Q||_F^2 <= sum_j k_c(m_j ||v_j||^2) + c^2 * b, where k_c(p) = c^2 - ((c-p)_+)^2 (so k_2: 0,3,4,4,...; k_3: 0,5,8,9,9,...). Its proof reuses the paper's Q = Q_+ - Q_- skeleton with von Neumann's trace inequality (proved from Birkhoff-von Neumann + rearrangement), plus two genuinely new generic tools: a Schur-Jensen step (sum_j g(Re M_jj) <= sum_i g(eigenvalue_i(M)) for PSD M and convex g via the doubly stochastic |U_ji|^2) and a spectrum-transfer lemma (sum g(lambda(W W^H)) = sum g(lambda(W^H W)) for ANY g with g(0)=0, via traces of powers + Lagrange interpolation). Applied at c=2 it yields 4 tr A-hat - ||A-hat||_F^2 - 2N(I') <= s1 (simple on-line zeros); at c=3 it yields 6 tr A-hat - ||A-hat||_F^2 - 3N(I') <= 2*#Z(I') = 2 N_d(I'). With the moment values these give 2-kappa(1)=2/3 and (3-kappa(1))/2=5/6. Crucially, TightMult.lean proves EQUALITY (lemmaR_tight) on configurations of orthonormal on-line atoms with integer 1 <= m_j <= c together with b pair-blocks Q = c*(projection): the certificate consuming only (tr, Frobenius norm, atom norms <= 1, n_+(Q) <= b) is exactly saturated, and at c=2 an on-line DOUBLE zero (k_2(2)=4) is indistinguishable from an off-line tight pair (c^2=4). Separately, PairCeiling proves a meta-theorem: EVERY bandwidth-one certificate of this shape (any C^1 weight r on [0,1]) certifies a simple-zero proportion at most 0.6818287 + 2.55e-6*(|r'(1)| + int|r''|) against an explicit 256-periodic near-CUE law (modulo externally-computed integer enclosures EnclOK), so Theorem D's optimal-window 0.67250 sits within ~0.009 of the provable ceiling of the entire method class.

key_items.name: ZeroConfig (abstract zero configuration)
key_items.statement: Structure: carrier set of DISTINCT points in closed strip 0<=Re<=1, mult : C -> N with mult>=1 on carrier, invariance under reflect(rho)=1-conj(rho) with mult(reflect rho)=mult(rho), finite in every ordinate window. NO arithmetic content; instantiated three times (zeta, Dirichlet L, xi'). Counting functions N, Nd, N0, N0star, N0s, Ns defined from it.

key_items.name: rank_trace_ineq (paper lem:ranktrace)
key_items.statement: P,Q Hermitian d x d over any RCLike field, P PSD with rank P <= r, n_+(Q) <= b, c>0: c*tr P - (c^2/4)*r + 2c*tr Q - c^2*b <= ||P+Q||_F^2. Proof: Q=Q_+-Q_-, drop tr(PQ_+)>=0, von Neumann on (P,Q_-), elementary scalar bounds x^2 >= cx - c^2/4 and x^2 >= 2cx - c^2. c=2 form: r >= 2 tr P + 4 tr Q - 4b - ||P+Q||_F^2.

key_items.name: Lemma R: rank_trace_mult / rank_trace_mult_k / rank_trace_mult_k_le
key_items.statement: For P = sum_j m_j v_j v_j^* (m_j >= 0 real), Q Hermitian, n_+(Q) <= b, c > 0: c*tr P + sum_j g_c(m_j ||v_j||^2) + 2c*tr Q - c^2 b <= ||P+Q||_F^2, with g_c(x) = x^2 - cx - ((x-c)_+)^2 (convex, C^1, g_c(0)=0, g_c >= -c^2/4). k-form: 2c*tr(P+Q) - ||P+Q||_F^2 <= sum_j k_c(m_j ||v_j||^2) + c^2 b, k_c(p) = c^2 - ((c-p)_+)^2 (concave, nondecreasing). Leak-free: if ||v_j||^2 <= 1 then RHS becomes sum_j k_c(m_j) + c^2 b. Integer values: k_2(1)=3, k_2(m>=2)=4; k_3(1)=5, k_3(2)=8, k_3(m>=3)=9.

key_items.name: Schur-Jensen + spectrum-transfer (the two generic tools inside Lemma R)
key_items.statement: sum_gc_diag_le_sum_gc_eigenvalues: for PSD M and c>=0, sum_j g_c(Re M_jj) <= sum_i g_c(lambda_i(M)) (Jensen along the doubly stochastic |U_ji|^2). sum_eigenvalues_comm: for ANY g:R->R with g(0)=0 and any rectangular W, sum_i g(lambda_i(W W^H)) = sum_j g(lambda_j(W^H W)) (Lagrange interpolation of g on the joint spectrum + tr((WW^H)^k) = tr((W^H W)^k)). Together they give tr g_c(P) >= sum_j g_c(m_j x_j): 'per-zero integrality survives interaction'.

key_items.name: lemmaR_tight / lemmaR_tight' / lemmaR_tight_two (TIGHTNESS)
key_items.statement: For every c>0: with r on-line atoms of integer multiplicities m_j <= c on ORTHONORMAL vectors (standard basis) and b pair-blocks Q = c * diag-projection onto b extra slots (n_+(Q) = b exactly, all Lemma-R hypotheses met exactly): 2c*tr(P+Q) - ||P+Q||_F^2 = sum_j k_c(m_j) + c^2*b, EQUALITY. At c=2: 4tr - ||.||^2 = 3*#{m=1} + 4*#{m>=2} + 4b, i.e. on-line double zeros (price 4) and off-line tight pairs at depth -> 0 (price c^2 = 4) are simultaneously extremal and provably indistinguishable by any certificate consuming only tr, ||.||_F^2, integer atoms on vectors of norm <= 1, and n_+(Q) <= p.

key_items.name: Sylvester subspace characterization (both directions)
key_items.statement: finrank_le_posIndex_of_posDefOn: any subspace on which x -> Re(x^H A x) is positive definite has dim <= n_+(A) (hard direction, via injectivity of A_+ on such a subspace). posDefOn_range_hermPosPart: the form IS pos-def on range(A_+), dim = n_+(A) (easy direction). Generalized version hermForm_gt_on_range_truncPos with threshold theta: form > theta*||x||^2 on range(specMap (t-theta)_+), dim = n_+^theta(A).

key_items.name: posIndex_conj_le + posIndex_add_le (lem:inertia)
key_items.statement: n_+(B^H Q B) <= n_+(Q) for Hermitian Q and any rectangular B (inertia under pull-back); n_+(Q1+Q2) <= n_+(Q1) + n_+(Q2) (subadditivity). Derived: posIndex_sub_le_rank: n_+(P - N) <= rank P for P,N PSD - this is exactly what prices each off-line hyperbolic pair-block at n_+ <= 1.

key_items.name: vonNeumann_trace_ineq
key_items.statement: For Hermitian A,B with decreasingly sorted eigenvalues a_i, b_i: Re tr(AB) <= sum_i a_i b_i. Proof from Birkhoff-von Neumann (Mathlib's exists_eq_sum_perm_of_mem_doublyStochastic) + rearrangement inequality; the doubly stochastic matrix is |{(U_A^H U_B)_kl}|^2.

key_items.name: weyl_posIndexAbove_le + cauchySchwarz_count (lem:weyl, lem:CS)
key_items.statement: Weyl: if all |lambda_i(E)| <= theta then n_+^theta(A+E) <= n_+(A) (tail absorption). CS count: for Hermitian R with tr R > theta*d: n_+^theta(R) >= (tr R - theta*d)^2 / tr(R^2). These two power the NON-multiplicity Cauchy-Schwarz forms (N0s/N >= 1/2, Nd/N >= 3/4) of Theorems B,C.

key_items.name: RH sanity anchors
key_items.statement: RH_implies_on_line: Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis puts every strip zero on Re = 1/2; RH_implies_all_on_line: under RH, N0 = N and N0* = N_d; trivial_chain: N0s <= N0* <= N0 <= N and N0s <= Ns <= Nd <= N. Definitions depend only on riemannZeta and analyticOrderAt (comparator/ChallengeDeps.lean, ~60 lines of trusted definitions).

result.bandwidth_role: Bandwidth enters at exactly three places, and it is the binding constraint everywhere. (1) The test family: the taper phi(u) = rho((L/2 - |u|)/w) has support EXACTLY [-L/2, L/2] with L = lambda*log(T/2pi) (Defs.lean, Params.phi), so the explicit-formula prime side P_X involves Lambda(n)/sqrt(n) only for n <= X = e^L = (T/2pi)^lambda - a Dirichlet polynomial of length T^lambda. The standing assumption Params.Valid forces 0 < lambda <= 1, and all headline theorems run lambda < 1 then lambda -> 1^-. lambda <= 1 is what unconditional mean-value technology (the Montgomery-Vaughan generalized Hilbert inequality, Zeta23/MV/, feeding the second-moment computation of thm:traces) can control: the second moment is ||G-hat||_F^2 <= (kappa(lambda) + o(1))*N with kappa(lambda) = 1/lambda + lambda/3 (kfun, FinalMult.lean), where 1/lambda is the diagonal/delta term and lambda/3 the form-factor integral. The certificate constant is 2 - kappa(lambda), increasing in lambda on (0,1], so the bandwidth cap lambda <= 1 yields exactly kappa(1) = 4/3 and the constants 2/3 (Thm A/B) and 5/6 (Thm C). (2) The tail: theta_0 ~ X^{1/2} log(4T)/D0^2 with D0 = sqrt(T) (TailInputs), and the error field calE contains X log l/(T l) + T^{lambda/2 - 1} - both need lambda bounded (lambda < 2 suffices here; the moments are the real constraint). (3) The ceiling: PairCeiling formalizes that the limitation is not an artifact of this proof - EVERY bandwidth-one certificate (weight r supported on the form-factor variable in [0,1], i.e., correlation information up to Dirichlet-polynomial length T) certifies at most 0.6818287 + 2.55e-6*(|r'(1)| + int|r''|) of simple zeros against the exhibited 256-periodic law. Two structural corollaries worth recording: unconstrained in lambda, H(lambda) = 2 - 1/lambda - lambda/3 is maximized at lambda = sqrt(3) with value 2 - 2/sqrt(3) ~ 0.8453, and by AM-GM kappa(lambda) >= 2/sqrt(3) > 1 for ALL lambda > 0 - so even granting arbitrary-length mean-value theorems, this second-moment certificate can never certify proportion 1; bandwidth relaxation alone caps at ~0.845.
limitations: Provable saturation of the certificate (lemmaR_tight, TightMult.lean): the inequality 2c*tr(P+Q) - ||P+Q||_F^2 <= sum_j k_c(m_j) + c^2*b is an EQUALITY on configurations of orthonormal on-line atoms (integer m_j <= c) plus b pair-blocks of eigenvalue c. No further inequality consuming only (tr G-hat, ||G-hat||_F^2, integer atoms on vectors of norm <= 1, n_+(Q) <= p) can improve the constants; at c=2 an on-line double zero and an off-line pair at depth -> 0 have identical certificate price (4).

Depth blindness: an off-line pair {rho, 1-conj(rho)} enters ONLY through the signature of its hyperbolic block 2m(xx^T - yy^T), i.e. n_+ <= 1, regardless of |beta - 1/2|. No norm information on off-line evaluation vectors is used or usable in this scheme; the method cannot localize or weigh off-line zeros, only bound the count p from above.

Second-moment barrier independent of bandwidth: kappa(lambda) = 1/lambda + lambda/3 >= 2/sqrt(3) ~ 1.1547 > 1 for all lambda > 0, so the certified proportion 2 - kappa is < 0.8453 always; certifying proportion 1 (RH) via this trace/Frobenius certificate is impossible for ANY Dirichlet-polynomial length, because the lambda/3 form-factor term is contributed by the zeros themselves (near-CUE randomness), not by technique deficiencies.

Bandwidth-one ceiling (PairCeiling): within lambda <= 1 the entire class of certificates of this shape is capped at 0.6818287 + 2.55e-6*(|r'(1)| + int|r''|) for the simple-zero proportion, so the headroom above Theorem D's 0.67250 is < 0.01; further progress within bandwidth one is nearly exhausted. Caveat: the ceiling instance carries the one displayed hypothesis EnclOK (256 integer enclosures produced by interval arithmetic OUTSIDE Lean, sha256-pinned); the analytic stability inequality itself is fully proved.

Proportion-only, asymptotic-only output: all results are liminf/epsilon-forms over dyadic windows (T,2T]; the effective constants c(lambda), loglog corrections of the paper are deliberately NOT formalized (Statement.lean: 'The effective c(lambda) forms are not stated'). No individual-zero statement, no zero-density statement off the line beyond the p-count.

The certificate cannot refute RH either: off-line pairs only decrease the left side of every inequality; there is no mechanism by which the certificate could certify the EXISTENCE of an off-line zero.

The Cauchy-Schwarz (non-multiplicity) route saturates strictly lower (1/2 and 3/4 instead of 2/3 and 5/6): the rank bound r in rank_trace_ineq leaks c^2/4 per atom; the multiplicity-aware k_c-form is the exact repair, and it is exactly tight (see item 1) - the improvement chain rank -> multiplicity-aware ends here.

The window variational problem is solved exactly (Montgomery-Taylor c1* = sqrt(2) tan(1/sqrt 2)/(1 + tan(1/sqrt 2)/sqrt 2)): no better taper/window exists within the one-window second-moment family; ThmD is the endpoint of that direction.
extension_hooks: Higher moments / new convex test functions: the Schur-Jensen lemma (sum_gc_diag_le_sum_gc_eigenvalues) and the spectrum-transfer lemma (sum_eigenvalues_comm, valid for ARBITRARY g with g(0)=0 via Lagrange interpolation) in RankTraceMult.lean are proved in full generality, not just for g_c. A third-moment certificate (tr G-hat^3, i.e. triple correlation sums on the prime side) could be dropped into the same skeleton; what is missing is a von Neumann-type inequality for the mixed term tr(P Q^2) and the prime-side asymptotics. This is the canonical way to break the lemmaR_tight saturation, since tightness is only proved relative to the quantity list (tr, ||.||_F^2, atom norms, n_+).

Quantitative inertia / depth pricing: n_+(Q) <= p discards the eigenvalue MAGNITUDES of the hyperbolic pair-blocks, which encode the depth |beta - 1/2| (and the norm of the off-line evaluation vectors). The thresholded index posIndexAbove(theta) and hermForm_gt_on_range_truncPos (Sylvester.lean) already exist for arbitrary theta; a 'weighted inertia' lemma bounding sum of positive eigenvalues of Q (not just their count) would price shallow off-line pairs above c^2 and strictly improve the certificate - the natural formal target for a novel method.

ZeroBlockData is instantiation-agnostic and already reused three times (zeta, Dirichlet L via ThmE, xi' via XiPrime): any locally finite multiset invariant under rho -> 1 - conj(rho) with sigma-equivariant evaluation vectors v(sigma z) = conj(v z) plugs in. A Hilbert-Polya-type candidate (spectral projections of a putative self-adjoint operator, or de Branges/Weil-positivity data) could feed the same posIndex/inertia certificate; the entire RHLinalg namespace (7 files, RCLike-generic, self-contained, no zeta content) is a ready-made library for any Hermitian-form positivity argument.

Bandwidth parameter lambda: the assembly (count_certificate) is parametric in kappa; ANY improvement in mean-value theorems for Dirichlet polynomials of length T^lambda, lambda > 1 (e.g. conditional on conjectural additive divisor estimates) immediately raises the constants through kfun with zero new formal work - up to the hard cap 2 - 2/sqrt(3) ~ 0.845 at lambda = sqrt(3).

ceiling_stability is configuration-free (no sign condition on the weights s_j): it can be re-run against ANY candidate form-factor law, making it a tool both for sharpening the ceiling (better laws, refined edge control of D(1), E(1)) and for stress-testing hypothetical counterexample configurations to RH against bandwidth-limited certificates. The N=256 instance shows the workflow: exact-rational certificate outside Lean -> integer enclosures -> kernel decide.

The free parameter c in Lemma R: currently only c=2 and c=3 are consumed. Non-integer c, or joint/family certificates combining several c-values against the same moments (the assembly already runs two counts in parallel), or c coupled to a multiplicity-dependent window, are unexplored; the k_c bookkeeping lemmas (sum_kc_two_nat, sum_kc_three_nat) generalize mechanically to any integer price table.

cauchySchwarz_count (n_+^theta(R) >= (tr R - theta d)^2 / tr R^2) is the crudest moment-to-count step; power-mean refinements using tr R^3 or restricted spectra would strengthen the non-multiplicity route and interact with hook 1.

The taper profile rho is an arbitrary C^3 monotone ramp (TaperProfile); ThmD optimizes one scalar window. Multi-window (matrix-valued weight over several grids), or windows adapted per zero-class (mollification/amplification in the vectors v_z rather than the scalar taper), would change the Gram structure while reusing prop:block verbatim - the block machinery only needs sigma-equivariance of the vectors.

result.summary:
Pages 16-35 of zeta-two-thirds.pdf contain: (i) the completion of the prime side (§5.3-5.5), (ii) the assembly of Theorems A-C (§6), (iii) the variants/limits section (§7) which is the richest source of pressure-point information, (iv) numerics (§8), and (v) Appendices A-C. The prime side computes tr G̃ and tr G̃² for the Gabor-Gram matrix G_kl = W(f_k,f_l) (f_k = φ(u)e^{-iτ_k u}, τ_k = T+2πk/L, d=⌊LT/2π⌋ frequencies, φ a C³ taper of support [-L/2,L/2], L=λl, l=log(T/2π)) purely from the explicit-formula density ν_X = μ + Π_X + P_X with primes n ≤ X = e^L = (T/2π)^λ. Lemma 5.4 reduces tr G̃² to a double integral M over I×I with error O(L·l·log l·(l²+X)); Props 5.5-5.7 evaluate the six bilinear pieces; the diagonal n=m of the prime-prime piece gives the main term (T/π)Σ_{n≤X}Λ(n)²g(log n)/n ~ TL³/6π, while the off-diagonal O₁ is killed by Montgomery-Vaughan (Lemma 5.2, constant 3π/2, with δ_n⁻¹ ≤ 2n giving O₁ ≪ L²X — this is THE step that pins λ ≤ 1). Theorem 5.8: tr G̃ = aL·N(T,2T)(1+O(E_T)), tr G̃² = (TL/2π)(ℓ₁²+L²/3)(1+O(E_T)), (tr G̃)²/tr G̃² = F(λ₁)N(1+O(E_T)), E_T := w/L + (l²+X)log l/(Tl) + T^{λ/2-1}. §6 then feeds these into the zero-side counting inequalities (Prop 4.4, from the rank-trace Lemma 3.2 applied to the block decomposition of Prop 4.1): N₀*, N₀ˢ ≥ (H(λ₁)-O(E'_T))N with H(λ)=2-1/λ-λ/3, and N_d ≥ (H_d(λ)-O(E'_T))N, H_d=(1+H)/2, giving 2/3, 2/3, 5/6 at λ=1; a Cauchy-Schwarz/Weyl branch (Lemma 3.3/3.4 + Prop 4.5) carries F(λ) for λ < 3-√6. The endpoint λ=1 is admissible because all secondary terms are o(main) even for X ≍ T (Remark 6.1).

§7 contains the optimality/limits material. §7.1: the window optimization is a Cauchy-Schwarz problem for 1+λ²T, maximizer v*_λ(s)=cos(√2 λs), c*_λ = √2 tanϑ/(1+ϑ tanϑ), ϑ=λ/√2; c*₁ = 0.7532960... is exactly the Montgomery-Taylor constant, and by [CCLM17, Cor 14] this solves the one-delta extremal problem using only F(α) on [-1,1]: "Theorem D is the limit of the method 'block structure + two traces + primes up to T': no window does better" (Theorem D: 2-1/c*₁ = 0.67250... on-line and simple, (3-1/c*₁)/2 = 0.83625... distinct). §7.2: orthonormalization is deliberately avoided — controlling Rayleigh quotients on small eigendirections of the mass matrix M would require bounds for P_X on intervals of length ≍ 1/L, i.e. Lindelöf-type information. §7.3+Remark 7.2: Theorem E (any fixed primitive χ) and the degree obstruction: for degree-m_F L-functions the certificate constant is c = Λ/(1+m_F Λ²/3) ≤ Λ* (Λ* = normalized max bandwidth forced by Montgomery-Vaughan, = 1/degree in the t-aspect), so the method is non-vacuous only if Λ* > 1/2: it is a degree-one method; an individual GL(2) L-function gives c = 6/13 < 1/2, i.e. nothing, whatever the window. §7.5 is the saturation analysis (see key items): dimension cap d = λ₁N (Prop 7.4), higher moments unconditionally unavailable/useless in the Rudnick-Sarnak range, the conditional moment program HL*(k₀,λ) reaching proportion 1 of simple on-line zeros but with the explicit disclaimer "RH itself is out of reach of the mechanism", and an RH-conditional distinct-zeros result 0.85082 from cubic weights. §7.4 places the result against Baluyot-Goldston-Suriajaya-Turnage-Butterbaugh/Goldston-Suriajaya: tr G̃² is the unconditional Fejér pair-correlation sum of [BGSTB24]/[GS26]; Lemma 3.2 replaces the termwise 'horizontal diagonal' positivity that fails off the line and reaches their target constants 2-C = 2/3 and (3-C)/2 = 5/6 unconditionally. Remark 7.3: applied to ξ′, the method gives unconditionally 0.85838 simple-on-line / 0.92919 distinct (flat window; 0.86864/0.93432 with quartic window v(s)=1-(7/100)(2s)²-(51/200)(2s)⁴) — Farmer-Gonek-Lee's RH-conditional 85.84% with RH removed.

The bandwidth-one ceiling (paper Remark 1.1, p.4, plus Lean Zeta23/PairCeiling/): an explicit extremal LAW — a finitely supported probability measure over 256-periodic marked configurations (rational weights, positions in [0,256), marks m ∈ {1,2} summing to 256), produced by an exact-rational LP — has grid form factor S(j) within τ = 3·10⁻⁴⁰ of the CUE/sine value j/256 for 0 < j < 256, edge discrepancy D(1) = ΣS(j)/256 - 1/2 ∈ [0, 0.82395317], and simple-point fraction exactly p₀ = 10909258999421303588095230195816054408197/16·10³⁹ = 0.68182868746.... The Lean stability inequality (ceiling_stability, two integrations by parts against C(x) = Σ_{j/N≤x}s_j, D = C-x²/2, E = ∫₀ˣD) shows every certificate (c₀,r) of the Theorem-B type — r ∈ C¹[0,1], r′ differentiable off a countable set with integrable derivative, valid against a configuration in the sense c₀ + Σ_j s_j r(j/N) ≤ p — has value c₀ + ∫₀¹ r(x)x dx ≤ p + |r(1)||D(1)| + |r′(1)||E(1)| + (sup|E|)∫₀¹|r″|; instantiated at the law (ceiling_law256_decimal / ceiling_law256_signed), v ≤ p₀ + 0.82395317|r(1)| + 2.5431316·10⁻⁶(|r′(1)| + ∫₀¹|r″|), and with r(1) ≥ 0 the edge term drops. Hence no bandwidth-one, configuration-by-configuration certificate certifies a simple-zero proportion above ≈ 0.6818287 + 2.55·10⁻⁶·(|r′(1)|+∫|r″|); Theorem B's 2/3 is within 0.016 of its own method's ceiling. result.bandwidth_role: Bandwidth enters at exactly four load-bearing points. (1) Support of the window: supp φ = [-L/2, L/2], L = λl, so Weil's formula for k = f∗g̃ (supp ⊂ [-L,L]) sees only prime powers n ≤ X = e^L = (T/2π)^λ — the certificate reads Montgomery's F(α) only for |α| ≤ λ ≤ 1 (Remark 5.10 makes this identification exact: tr G̃² ↔ ∫_{-λ}^{λ}(λ-|α|)F(α)dα = λ+λ³/3). (2) The Montgomery-Vaughan step (Lemma 5.2 with δ_n⁻¹ ≤ 2n, giving off-diagonal O₁ ≪ L²X in Prop 5.6) is what makes the prime-side second moment unconditional, and it collapses for X ≫ Tl: beyond λ = 1 the off-diagonal requires Hardy-Littlewood prime-pair correlations, equivalently Montgomery's conjecture for α > 1 (§7.5(a)). λ = 1 itself is admissible only because every secondary term is o(main) even at X ≍ T (Remark 6.1). (3) Dimension: the test family has d = ⌊LT/2π⌋ = λ₁N+O(1) elements at the critical Gabor density h = 2π/L, and rank/positive-index certificates can never certify more than d points (Prop 7.4 Cap) — so the same bandwidth that limits the prime side also caps the certifiable proportion at λ₁·100%, and makes the certificate vacuous for λ ≤ 1/2. For higher-degree L-functions the forced normalized bandwidth Λ* = 1/degree puts GL(2) below the vacuity threshold (Remark 7.2). (4) The ceiling: the PairCeiling development shows that the bandwidth-one data itself (form-factor measure on [0,1], i.e. masses s_j at j/256 within 3·10⁻⁴⁰ of CUE, plus edge mass) is consistent with a genuine configuration law whose simple fraction is 0.68182868746..., so within bandwidth one no certificate of the paper's linear type can exceed ≈0.6818287 — the binding constraint is not the linear algebra (Lemma 3.2 is tight) nor the window (Montgomery-Taylor is optimal, Theorem D + [CCLM17]) but the bandwidth of the arithmetic input. Higher moments do not help within the bandwidth: tr G̃^k is computable only in the Rudnick-Sarnak range kλ < 2 (§7.5(e)).
limitations: Hard ceiling within the method's data class: no certificate (c₀,r) reading only bandwidth-one pair data (form-factor/pair-correlation with Fourier support in [-1,1] plus mean density plus multiplicity integrality), valid configuration-by-configuration, certifies simple-on-line proportion > 0.6818287 + 2.55·10⁻⁶·(|r′(1)|+∫|r″|) — because an explicit 256-periodic law of marked configurations realizes near-CUE pair data with simple fraction exactly 0.68182868746.... 2/3 is within 0.016 of this cap. IMPORTANT scope caveat: the ceiling as formalized rules out certificates that are (i) linear in the form factor, (ii) with weight r ∈ C¹, r′ of bounded variation (the error budget scales with |r′(1)|+∫|r″|, so wilder r escapes the stated bound only by blowing the error term), and (iii) valid against every configuration sharing the data (in particular against the law's average). It does NOT rule out: arguments using arithmetic information specific to ζ beyond the shared data (mollifiers/Levinson-Conrey machinery, moments of ζ, zero-density, amplification); higher-correlation (k≥3) inputs, which the 256-law was not built to match; bandwidth > 1; family averaging; nonlinear functionals of the spectral data; or, of course, anything about disproving RH.

λ ≤ 1 is essential and not an artifact: for X ≫ Tl the off-diagonal prime sums need Hardy-Littlewood-strength prime-pair information (= Montgomery pair correlation for α > 1). The quantified cost of going further: proportions 0.70/0.80/0.90 need Fourier support ≈ 1.04/1.26/1.70 (Remark 1.1).

Prop 7.4 (Cap): the whole architecture (rank/index of a d-dimensional compression) certifies at most d = λ₁N points; nothing for λ ≤ 1/2; hence 100% is the absolute ceiling even with all moments, and the method structurally 'does not distinguish two thirds from all' — it produces lower bounds only, insensitive to o(N) off-line zeros.

The inputs (functional equation, explicit formula, mean values of length-≤T Dirichlet polynomials) are satisfied by Davenport-Heilbronn and Epstein zeta functions for which RH is FALSE (§1.5); therefore no refinement of these inputs alone can prove RH. The paper states flatly for the conditional moment program: 'RH itself is out of reach of the mechanism' (§7.5(f)) — even HL*(k₀,λ) for all k₀ gives only proportion 1 of simple on-line zeros (a density-one statement), not RH.

Higher moments are unconditionally unavailable: tr G̃^k evaluable only for kλ < 2 (Rudnick-Sarnak); for λ ∈ (1/2,1) only k ≤ 3 (and only λ < 2/3), and odd moments do not improve the Christoffel bound; for λ ≤ 1/2 where many moments exist, the Cap makes them useless. So the two-trace certificate is provably the best unconditional one in this family.

The linear algebra is exhausted: Lemma 3.2 is tight (lemmaR_tight, kernel-checked equality case), Prop 4.4 is sharp in all three parts at the Montgomery extremal configuration (2/3 simple + 1/6 doubles/deep pairs), and the window optimization is closed (Montgomery-Taylor optimal by [CCLM17 Cor 14]). No slack anywhere except the arithmetic input.

Degree-one method: individual GL(2) L-functions give c = 6/13 < 1/2, i.e. literally nothing, whatever the window; positive output needs normalized bandwidth Λ* > 1/2 (Λ* > 3-√6 = 0.5505 for a nonvacuous on-line proportion at degree 1).

Orthonormalizing the test family (to get genuine eigenvalue counts rather than inertia) is blocked: it would require control of P_X on intervals of length ≍ 1/log T, i.e. Lindelöf-type information (Remark 7.1(ii)).
Effectivity is asymptotic-only: the certificate is strictly negative at all computationally accessible heights (Remark 5.9, §8 tables); convergence is 1-O(1/log X).

In Lean, the ceiling theorems carry the one hypothesis EnclOK (the 256 enclosures, produced by external 70-digit interval arithmetic; certificate JSON not in the repository — only its sha256), so the 0.6818287 figure is machine-checked modulo that finite computation; the paper's Remark 1.1 rounds it to 0.68185 and does not prove it in the text.
extension_hooks: The 0.0152 gap between 2/3 (resp. 0.67250 with the optimal window) and the 0.68182868746 cap is genuine room WITHIN bandwidth one: the paper's certificate is not extremal against the 256-law. Closing it means optimizing (c₀, r) against all bandwidth-one configurations — an infinite-dimensional LP whose dual is the law; the Lean stability machinery (Stability.lean/Ceiling.lean, configuration-free) is exactly the verification harness for any improved certificate.

Quantified bandwidth targets: pair-correlation input on support [0, 1.04] would already beat the cap (0.70); 1.26 → 0.80, 1.70 → 0.90. Any partial unconditional information beyond α = 1 (e.g. averaged Hardy-Littlewood, almost-all-h prime-pair asymptotics, or the α > 1 lower bounds of Goldston-Montgomery type) plugs directly into O₁ of Prop 5.6 — the sole obstruction is one off-diagonal bilinear form over prime pairs with |log(n/m)| small.

The fourth-moment lever: HL*(4,λ) (a single additive-correlation asymptotic Σ_m(Λ*Λ)(m)(Λ*Λ)(m+h), |h| ≤ X²/T) yields 13/18 = 0.7222 via the Christoffel function Λ₂(0;1) = 5/36 — a concrete, well-posed conjecture strictly weaker than full pair correlation with extended support. The general moment-to-count machine (§7.5(d): n₊/d ≥ 1-Λ_m(0), Chebyshev-Markov-Stieltjes) is set up and waiting for any new moment input; it also invites SDP/LP duality analysis (cf. CGdL20) at the level of moment sequences.

Family averaging (Remark 7.2(iii)): both tr and ‖·‖²_F are linear, so the whole certificate commutes with averaging over families; orthogonality of characters restores Λ* = 1 for {χ mod q}, promising 2/3 on-line/simple for almost all χ with T as small as a power of log q. The stated missing ingredient is a Gevrey-class taper in Prop 4.2 (better tail decay of φ̂ off the real axis) — a purely technical, self-contained analytic problem. Same lever could give GL(2) families (where individuals are hopeless) a positive proportion.

The rank-trace inequality is tight only for the listed invariants (tr, ‖·‖_F, block structure, tr P₁ ≤ s₁): lemmaR_tight is an invitation to add invariants. Candidates visible in the setup: the operator norm of Ĝ (an off-line pair of depth y contributes eigenvalues ≍ ±X^{|y|}... self-pair term ≍ X^{|2β-1|}, p.11 remark — any unconditional upper bound on λ_max(Ĝ) would penalize deep off-line pairs and split the 'flat charge 4'), localized/windowed traces (tr against several windows simultaneously = a matrix-valued moment problem), and traces against shifted grids (the pair blocks' individual traces are currently unconstrained).

The two levels of integrality (m-1)² ≥ 0 and (m-1)(m-2) ≥ 0 are used; §7.5(g) shows the cubic level (LP over span{m, m², m³, 1_{m=1}}) works under RH via Schur-Horn majorization. A systematic majorization calculus for higher integrality polynomials against available (or conjectured) traces is a mechanizable research direction — the Lean LinAlg layer (von Neumann, Sylvester, Weyl) is the reusable core.

ξ′ and beyond: the two-trace transfer to ξ′ (0.85838/0.92919 unconditional, formalized) suggests iterating to ξ^{(k)} (Farmer-Gonek program: proportions →1 as k→∞) and asking whether the rank-trace device transfers with quantitative gain per derivative; the quartic window v(s) = 1-(7/100)(2s)²-(51/200)(2s)⁴ shows window re-optimization is object-specific (the ThmD variational problem changes with the density J).

The Kreĭn-space reading (Appendix C.3, Bombieri [Bom00], Yoshida [Yos92]): W on the full space is positive iff RH; the paper extracts what TWO moments of ANY finite compression certify. The open structural question it isolates: what functional-analytic invariant of the compression sequence (beyond moments — e.g. the full spectral measure of G̃, its operator-norm growth, or the Toeplitz/Gabor structure of M^{-1/2}GM^{-1/2} conditional on Lindelöf) is both unconditionally computable from primes and sensitive to a single off-line zero. Remark 7.1(ii) pinpoints the exact analytic threshold: bounds for P_X on windows of length 1/log T.

The hybrid regime q ≤ T^ϑ (Remark 7.2(i)): claimed to give H(1/(1+ϑ)) uniformly (positive for ϑ < √6/3 ≈ 0.816) modulo checking uniformity of error terms — a low-risk verification project with new content (proportion results uniform in conductor).

The extremal-law construction itself (exact-rational LP over N-periodic marked configurations, interval-arithmetic enclosures, kernel-checked row certificates) is a reusable template for computing ceilings of OTHER certificate classes: adding a third-moment row set to the LP would compute the exact ceiling of the two-trace + triple-correlation method (conditionally relevant per §7.5(g)), quantifying precisely how much each new arithmetic input is worth before attempting to prove it.

result.bandwidth_role: The band-limit L = λ·log(T/2π) of the test functions (supp f ⊂ [−L/2, L/2], so the Weil form W(f,g) = Σ_ρ m_ρ h_f(γ_ρ)h_g(γ̄_ρ) is computable from primes ≤ X = e^L = (T/2π)^λ alone) is THE resource parameter of the whole method, and every ceiling in the material is a bandwidth statement. (1) Dimension cap: the Gabor test space at critical sampling density has d = λ·N(T,2T)(1+o(1)) atoms, and rank P, n_+^θ(G̃) ≤ d, so no certificate of this kind can certify more than λN on-line points — 100% at λ=1, nothing at λ ≤ 1/2 (paper Prop. 7.4, p. 24). (2) The restriction λ ≤ 1 is forced by the Montgomery–Vaughan generalized Hilbert inequality: the off-diagonal prime sums in tr G̃² are O(L²X log X), dominated by the diagonal T·L³/6π only for X = o(T·L); beyond λ=1 one needs Hardy–Littlewood prime-pair correlations (= Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture for |α| > 1). Within λ ≤ 1 the second moment is unconditionally (tr R)²/tr R² = λN/(1+λ²/3)(1+o(1)) — Montgomery's F(α) on |α| ≤ 1 for complex zeros (BGSTB 2024). (3) Higher moments tr R^k are diagonal-dominated only in the Rudnick–Sarnak range kλ < 2: k=3 is admissible for λ < 2/3 but odd moments provably cannot improve a count on [0,∞) without a λ_max bound (Lindelöf-strength control of Σ_{n≤X} Λ(n)n^{−1/2−iτ} on windows of length 1/L); k=4 needs λ < 1/2, where the dimension cap already kills everything (transcript pp. 80–81; paper §7.5(d),(e)). (4) The formalized 'bandwidth-one ceiling' (Zeta23/PairCeiling/) is literally the statement that ANY certificate (c₀, r) reading only the form factor S(j) on the grid j/N ⊂ [0,1] (i.e. pair-correlation data of Fourier support ≤ 1) and valid configuration-by-configuration certifies a simple-zero proportion ≤ 0.6818287 + 2.55·10⁻⁶·(|r′(1)| + ∫|r″|). (5) The constants themselves are bandwidth functions: H(λ) = 2 − 1/λ − λ/3 (nontrivial iff λ > 3−√6 = 0.5505), F(λ) = λ/(1+λ²/3); Remark 1.1: reaching 0.70/0.80/0.90 by this route needs pair-correlation support out to ≈ 1.04/1.26/1.70. (6) In Part I's visibility analysis, the resolution 1/L governs when off-line zeros become spectrally visible at all (annihilation threshold, cluster resolution ε ≳ 0.2·2π/L).
extension_hooks: Strengthen the sole analytic input: everything downstream of the rank–trace lemma is fed by ONE unconditional asymptotic — tr G̃² = (1/λ + λ/3)N(1+o(1)), i.e. Montgomery's F(α) for complex zeros on |α| ≤ 1 (BGSTB 2024, Thm 1). Any extension of unconditional pair correlation to support 1+δ propagates linearly: proportion = 2 − (second-moment constant). Paper Remark 1.1 quantifies: support 1.04 → 0.70, 1.26 → 0.80, 1.70 → 0.90. This is the cleanest single target (transcript p. 24 note; paper pp. 3, 24).

The gap 2/3 (achieved, flat window) → 0.67250 (Montgomery–Taylor, optimal window — proved optimal given F on [−1,1] and two traces) → 0.68183 (bandwidth-one ceiling, all certificates) is only 0.016 wide but structurally interesting: the ceiling allows certificates strictly better than the two-trace optimum, using richer functionals of bandwidth-one data. The Lean ceiling_law256 slack terms |r′(1)| and ∫|r″| show exactly what a certificate pays for curvature; Signed.lean (ceiling_nearCUE_signed) prices signed weights. Constructing a certificate between 0.6725 and 0.68183, or proving the true sup, is a well-posed finite-dimensional problem (Zeta23/PairCeiling/, paper Remark 1.1).

The Lindelöf lock: an a-priori bound λ_max(G̃/ℓ₁) = O(1) — equivalently bounds for P_X(τ) = Σ_{n≤X}Λ(n)n^{−1/2−iτ} on windows of length ≍ 1/L — would (a) unlock the third moment tr R³ (admissible for λ < 2/3) as a useful constraint and (b) permit orthonormalisation of the Gabor family (paper Remark 7.1(ii), re-derivation agent's Remark 7.4). This is a concrete sub-Lindelöf statement about short-window means of Dirichlet polynomials, weaker than Lindelöf itself; nobody in the campaign attempted it directly.

Conditional moment ladder as intermediate targets (paper §7.5(f)): HL*(4, λ) — a single Hardy–Littlewood-type asymptotic for Σ_m (Λ*Λ)(m)(Λ*Λ)(m+h), |h| ≤ X²/T, giving tr G̃⁴ its sine-kernel value m₄(1)=13/4 — yields ≥ 13/18 = 0.7222 simple on-line via the Christoffel function Λ₂(0;1) = 5/36; HL*(k,λ) for all k gives proportion → 1 (100% simple on the line), the mechanism's absolute ceiling. Each finite level is a precise additive-correlation statement one could attack by circle-method/dispersion innovations.

Family averaging (paper Remark 7.2(iii)): both tr and ‖·‖_F² commute with averaging over families (the rank–trace lemma is linear in these), and orthogonality of characters restores effective bandwidth Λ* = 1 for the family of all χ mod q, q → ∞ — expected: 2/3 on the line on average for T as small as a power of log q. Needs a Gevrey-class taper in Prop 4.2; explicitly NOT carried out. Same for the hybrid range q ≤ T^θ giving H(1/(1+θ)) (uniformity unchecked). A GL(2) family version would be genuinely new since the individual GL(2) case gives nothing (c = 6/13 < 1/2).

The rank–trace lemma's tightness theorem (Zeta23/ZeroSide/TightMult.lean, lemmaR_tight) is tightness ONLY against the information {on-line atoms with integer multiplicities ≤ c on orthonormal vectors, b pair-blocks of eigenvalue c}: 2c·tr(P+Q) − ‖P+Q‖_F² = Σ_j k_c(m_j) + c²b. New global invariants not in this list — e.g. commutator traces tr[P,Q]², off-diagonal block correlations, the translation structure of the Gabor grid (Toeplitz/Szegő asymptotics of G̃), or positivity of F(α) outside [−1,1] (the Chirre–Gonçalves–de Laat regime, explicitly scoped out of Theorem D's optimality) — are not covered by any stated obstruction.

The ξ′ transfer (paper Remark 7.3, Zeta23/XiPrime/): the rank–trace device applied to the Farmer–Gonek–Lee explicit formula for ξ′/ξ removes RH from their 85.84% and the quartic window beats it (86.864% simple, 93.432% distinct). Iterating to ξ^(j) and feeding Farmer/Wu-style distinct-zero bootstraps is unexplored; per-problem window optimization (the quartic window 1 − (7/100)(2s)² − (51/200)(2s)⁴ beat the flat one) suggests a family of tractable variational problems.

The de Branges δ-tilt (transcript p. 48, recorded but never developed): E_a(z) = ξ(a − iz), kernel K_a with exactly κ_a negative squares = N(β > a) counted WITH multiplicity — unlike the Weil form, where multiplicity is invisible (Theorem 1). If a prime-computable (rather than Riemann–Siegel-computable) compression of K_a existed, it would see multiplicities; the run identified d/da log|ξ(a+it)/ξ(1−a+it)| at a = 1/2 with 2πν_X. Making the K_a compressions arithmetic is an open structural problem.

Part I's ledger for the positive-index route: any prime-side proof that a fraction 1−η of eigenvalues of the level-(T/2π) compressed Weil form exceed θ gives proportion ≥ 1−2η on the line (under RH the truth is η = 0: all d = N eigenvalues positive — 'semi-local Weil positivity'). Eigenvalue-counting beyond two moments, e.g. via the Chebyshev–Markov–Stieltjes/Christoffel framework (paper §7.5(d)) with any new computable functional, plugs in here at rate +2η (transcript p. 39).

Campaign residue worth mining: (i) the empirical e^{−4πX} Weil-positivity margin law with mechanism located in Connes–Consani prolate spheroidal eigenvalue leakage — a quantitative object for any attempt to push Weil positivity past supp [1/3, 3] (certified there by interval arithmetic, primes 2,3,5,7); (ii) the three thin-interval zero-density improvements from a dropped 1979 Heath-Brown lemma (confirmed by two referees, never written up); (iii) the barrier-checker methodology (R0/new-7): a zoo of RH-false model worlds (Epstein class number 2, Davenport–Heilbronn, Beurling with planted zeros, fake Weil polynomials) that mechanically classifies proposed methods by which model kills them — a reusable discipline for the follow-up program (transcript pp. 5–15).

The interference obstruction of Part I (pp. 31–33) is stated for the specific bump construction; the measured laws L*_ann ≈ 1.12·δ^{−0.07}·log(t₀/2π)^{0.89} and L*_rob ≈ 1.6·δ^{−0.34}·log(t₀/2π)^{0.6} are empirical fits. A configuration-free visibility theorem is argued impossible via an uncertainty-principle heuristic ('BLe^{yu}/c(yL) is a probability density...'), not a proof; a rigorous impossibility theorem, or a visibility theorem under a mild density hypothesis on off-line zeros, is open.
limitations: Dimension cap (paper Prop. 7.4, 'trivial but decisive'): rank P₁ ≤ rank P ≤ d and n_+^θ(G̃) ≤ d = λ₁N + O(1), so NO argument based on compressions with test support [−L/2, L/2], L = λl can certify more than λ₁N on-line points; the certificate of Prop 4.4(ii) is ≤ (2 − 1/λ₁ + o(1))N and non-positive for λ ≤ 1/2.

λ ≤ 1 is essential: for X ≫ Tl the Montgomery–Vaughan off-diagonal no longer dominates and evaluation requires Hardy–Littlewood prime-pair information (equivalently Montgomery's PCC for α > 1). The method's 100%-ceiling at λ=1 is unreachable without it.

Bandwidth-one ceiling (formalized, Zeta23/PairCeiling/CeilingLaw256.lean; paper Remark 1.1): every certificate of the Theorem-B type reading only bandwidth-one pair-correlation data configuration-by-configuration certifies ≤ 0.6818287 + 2.55·10⁻⁶·(|r′(1)| + ∫|r″|) simple zeros. 2/3 is within 0.016 of this; the remaining gap to 1 is structural, not technical.

Higher moments are provably useless unconditionally: tr R³ computable for λ < 2/3 but an odd moment cannot improve a lower bound for a count on [0,∞) (mass at height h → ∞ feeds m₃ freely; LP-dual: cubic certificates dominated by quadratic) absent a λ_max = O(1) bound, which is Lindelöf-strength; tr R⁴ needs λ < 1/2 where d < N/2 kills everything ('Theorem U' of the E2-HL agent; transcript pp. 80–81, paper §7.5(e)).

No bearing on RH in either direction: the inputs (functional equation, explicit formula, mean values of Dirichlet polynomials of length ≤ T) are insensitive to o(N) off-line zeros and are satisfied by RH-false objects (Davenport–Heilbronn, Epstein class number > 1). 'Nothing in the method distinguishes between two thirds and all' (paper §1.5, §7.5(a)). Even the full conditional moment ladder HL*(k,λ) ∀k gives 100% simple on-line but 'RH itself is out of reach of the mechanism' (§7.5(f)).

The negative-index (Pontryagin) route to counting off-line zeros is EMPTY for structural reasons: κ(V) ≤ N^dist_off is the wrong direction; the reverse needs visibility of all zeros below T, which needs dim V ≳ N(T), where κ ≤ dim V is trivial; the honest compressed index is identically 0 for X = 10²..10⁶, T ≤ 2400 while sign-based predictions give hundreds (R4's 33–153 negatives were an artifact of the warped-sinc operator, not a Weil-form compression). Multiplicity is intrinsically invisible to the Weil form's signature (Theorem 1: κ counts DISTINCT off-line zeros); clusters count once; no configuration-free visibility theorem exists (transcript Part I, pp. 16, 32–35, 47–53).

Per-pair 'integrality' pricing is false: every quadratic per-pair inequality with free mass or free phase fails (G1–G4 experiments, gaps −0.25 to −4.0); phase-locking is forced by the functional equation + Poisson, but free magnitude still kills it (degenerate pairs with v^Tv → 0, A → ∞ act as free mass movers). Only the mass-linear rank–trace inequality survives — the (m−1)² ≥ 0 level; the (m−1)(m−2) ≥ 0 spectral level is destroyed by interactions (eigenvalues of interacting simple zeros fill (0,2); false already under RH+GUE where the Gram spectrum has variance 1/3) — the paper recovers it only by the regrouping device (P₁, Q′), not spectrally (transcript pp. 68–71, 81; paper §7.5(c)).

Orthonormalisation is blocked: the Gabor mass matrix is Toeplitz with symbol taking every value in [0,1], so ≍ ηd eigenvalues are small and on bad eigendirections the Rayleigh quotient is controlled only by sup|P_X| ∼ √X — Lindelöf-type input needed. The published argument avoids orthonormalisation entirely (coefficient coordinates); this restricts which spectral statistics are accessible (paper Remark 7.1(ii)).

Degree-one method: for an L-function of degree m with Λ* := lim log T/log q(T), c ≤ Λ*, so non-vacuous only for Λ* > 3−√6; individual GL(2) (Λ* = 1/2) gives c = 6/13 < 1/2 — nothing, for any window (paper Remark 7.2(ii)). Davenport–Heilbronn-type functions (no Euler product): Σ|c(n)|² grows like x^{1+δ}, Prop 5.6 fails, certificate empty — the correct RH-false control behavior.

Montgomery–Taylor optimality: c₁* = 0.7532961 is the exact sup of the variational functional; by CCLM17 Cor. 14 no window does better given only F on [−1,1], so Theorem D (0.67250) is the limit of 'block structure + two traces + primes up to T'. Improvements need either F outside [−1,1] or non-two-trace functionals (paper §7.1).

The de Branges/K_a route: compressions computable only from ξ on vertical lines (Riemann–Siegel, not primes); negative index bounded below only by resolved Blaschke windings (≈ samples needed per zero); no positive-index dual exists because positive squares of K_a are not tied to a zero count (transcript p. 48).

Simplicity via rank alone caps at 1/3 in the direct Part-II route (N^simple ≥ 2n^dist_on − N_on); the paper's 2/3-simple (Theorem B) needs the regrouping; further simplicity gains need the (m−1)(m−2) level, destroyed spectrally by interactions.

Campaign-level wall (coordinator's synthesis of ~30 refuted attempts): the only axiom set not barred by an explicit RH-false model is the full one (functional equation + Euler product at every prime + Ramanujan), and every attempted route's first substantive step turned out to be Weil positivity or an equivalent in disguise (transcript p. 8).

Caveats of the record itself: the transcript volume's mathematics 'has not been independently verified'; the campaign's referees were all Claude instances ('The next reader should be a person'); several literature constants were recalled from memory; the PairCeiling result rests on the one hypothesis EnclOK (256 integer enclosures produced by interval arithmetic outside Lean, sha256 cc3de991...).
result.summary:
The file zeta-transcript-explanation.pdf (95 pp., 'How the two-thirds argument was found') is Claude's own rewritten account — compiled from complete logs, explicitly NOT independently verified — of the two-day, ~60-subagent campaign that produced the paper. Structure: a coordinator's overview (pp. 4–15: one orchestrating thread, one human giving one-line prompts, sub-agents launched with written research-memo briefs including RH-false control cases, hostile blind referees for every claimed theorem); Part I (pp. 15–53), the 'one-half run' (agent E2); Part II (pp. 54–81), the 'two-thirds run' (agent E2-pairs); and a literature-provenance appendix (pp. 83–95) establishing that no downloaded paper supplied any lemma, inequality, constant, or proof step on the whole chain — both core runs made zero network requests, and the decisive tools (pullback inertia, von Neumann's trace inequality, the Montgomery–Vaughan reduction, the variational c* = 0.7532961) were recalled from training or invented in-run. The document is exceptionally rich in negative results: ~30 refuted attack directions in the first waves (Weil positivity variants, Jensen polynomials, de Bruijn–Newman, Lee–Yang lifts, Langlands amplification ceilings, archimedean Euler systems, etc.), converging on the coordinator's stated wall: 'the only axiom set not barred by some explicit RH-false model is the full one (functional equation, Euler product at every prime, Ramanujan), and every route's first substantive step turned out to be Weil positivity or an equivalent in disguise.'

Part I's arc: the brief proposed a Pontryagin-space route — bound the negative index κ of prime-computable compressions of the Weil Hermitian form W(f,g) = Σ_ρ m_ρ h_f(γ_ρ)h_g(γ̄_ρ) to upper-bound off-line zeros. E2 proved Theorem 1 (κ on C_c^∞ = number of DISTINCT zeros with Re ρ > 1/2; multiplicity invisible; RH ⇔ κ(L) = 0 ∀L — the negative-index half already in Bombieri 2000), then showed the route is structurally empty: the honest compressed index is identically 0 across X = 10²…10⁶, T ≤ 2400 (computed from primes alone), κ(V) ≤ N^dist_off is the wrong inequality direction, visibility of all zeros needs dim V ≳ N(T) where κ ≤ dim V is trivial, and interference makes any configuration-free visibility theorem impossible. The prior run R4's '33–153 negative eigenvalues' were an artifact of a warped-sinc operator that is not a compression of W. E2 then inverted the mechanism: pullback inertia n₊(A*QA) ≤ n₊(Q), an off-line pair {ρ, 1−ρ̄} being a signature-(1,1) block counted TWICE by Riemann–von Mangoldt, gives N₀^dist(I′) ≥ 2n₊^θ(W|V) − N(I′); Cauchy–Schwarz gives n₊ ≥ (tr R)²/tr R², and the unconditional Montgomery–Vaughan-range evaluation (tr R)²/tr R² = λN/(1+λ²/3)(1+o(1)) yields ≥ 1/2 distinct on-line at λ = 1 (= 2·(3/4) − 1: 'inertia removes the need for RH at the price 3/4 → 1/2').

Part II's arc: the brief handed E2-pairs Montgomery's integer template (m² ≥ 2m−1 ⇒ 2/3 simple under RH; 5/6 distinct; 5/6 through the double count = exactly 2/3), diagnosed that E2 had 'lost integrality' passing from integer multiplicities to real eigenvalues, but forecast the recovery wrongly (higher prime-side moments). The run found by extremal experiments that every per-pair quadratic pricing fails — free phase gives zero-cost pair blocks (v = e^{−iπ/4}r), free magnitude gives degenerate 'free mass movers' — so the correct inequality must be LINEAR in the masses: the rank–trace inequality (paper Lemma 3.2, Lean RankTrace.lean:163): for P ⪰ 0 of rank ≤ r and Hermitian Q with n₊(Q) ≤ b, c·tr P − c²r/4 + 2c·tr Q − c²b ≤ ‖P+Q‖²_F, proved in five lines via von Neumann's trace inequality; at c = 2, r ≥ 2 tr P + 4 tr Q − 4b − ‖P+Q‖²_F. Applied to the windowed zero-side matrix with only |u_i|² ≤ 1 (from the exact Poisson identity Σ_k φ̂(z−τ_k)φ̂(z′−τ_k) = LΦ(z−z′)), it yields n^dist_on(I′) ≥ 4 tr A − 2N(I′) − ‖A‖²_F ≥ (2 − 1/λ − λ/3 − o(1))N → (2/3)N — no pair data needed at all. The run was killed mid-write by an infrastructure error; the coordinator checked the orphaned proof line-by-line and resumed it. The accompanying paper (zeta-two-thirds.pdf, 35 pp.) and sorry-free Lean formalization (zeta-23-lean-main, Theorems A–E plus ξ′ results and the bandwidth-one ceiling) carry the polished statements, the Montgomery–Taylor optimization (Theorem D, 0.67250), the Dirichlet extension (Theorem E), and §7.5's remarkably candid 'limits of the method' — the primary quarry for a follow-up program.

key_items.name: Document identity and caveat
key_items.statement: The transcript-explanation volume is Claude's own account of the campaign, rewritten from logs; 'the mathematics in this volume... has not been independently verified; this caveat concerns this volume only, not the accompanying paper.' ~60 sub-agents; 54-hour session; agents saw only their briefs; hostile blind referees for every claimed theorem; final verdict 'The next reader should be a person.'

key_items.name: Theorem 1 (negative index of Weil form)
key_items.statement: κ(W on C_c^∞) = #{distinct zeros with Re ρ > 1/2}; an m-fold off-line zero contributes exactly ONE negative square (multiplicity invisible); κ(L) := κ on supp ⊂ [−L/2, L/2] is finite, nondecreasing, → κ; RH ⇔ κ(L) = 0 for all L. Negative-index half attributed to Bombieri 2000.

key_items.name: Empirical: honest compressed index is identically zero
key_items.statement: Inertia of the prime-side Gram matrix G_P of W on Gabor spaces: n₋ = 0 for every X = 10², 10³, 10⁴, 10⁵, 10⁶ on windows [50,1000] (639 zeros) and [1400,2400] (907 zeros), min eigenvalue at leakage level ~10⁻⁶–10⁻⁸, while ν_X < 0 on 21–42% of the window and Szegő/a-priori sign counts predict 65–746 negatives. R4's 33–153 negatives belong to the warped-sinc kernel sin(π(N_X(t)−N_X(s)))/(π(t−s)), not to any compression of W.

key_items.name: Visibility theorem and its obstructions
key_items.statement: An isolated off-line zero of depth δ at height t is visible (forces a negative square) once log X ≥ C√(log t)/δ — but only under hypothesis (HR) (no other off-line zeros within R = e^{L/8}) because of an uncontrolled e^{L/4} interference loss; clusters within o(1/L) count once (at most 2); measured annihilation threshold L*_ann ≈ 1.12·δ^{−0.07}·log(t₀/2π)^{0.89}, robust threshold L*_rob ≈ 1.6·δ^{−0.34}·log(t₀/2π)^{0.6}; 'no configuration-free visibility theorem exists.'

key_items.name: The dual mechanism (one-half theorem, = paper's Cauchy–Schwarz branch)
key_items.statement: n₊(A*QA) ≤ n₊(Q) (2-line proof); off-line pair = block [[0,m],[m,0]] of signature (1,1), counted twice by RvM: N(I′) ≥ n^dist_on + 2n^dist_pair; hence N₀^dist(I′) ≥ 2n₊^θ(W|V) − N(I′); n₊ ≥ (tr R − θd)²₊/tr R² (prime-computable); (tr R)²/tr R² = λN/(1+λ²/3)(1+o(1)) unconditionally for λ ≤ 1 via Montgomery–Vaughan (off-diag/diag = O(X log X/(|I|L²)) = O(T^{λ−1}/l)); at λ=1: ≥ (1/2 − o(1))N distinct on-line. Prime-only numerics: C/N = 0.766/0.762/0.757 at T = 10⁴/5·10⁴/10⁶ vs. law 0.750.

key_items.name: Rank–trace inequality (the lever; 'Lemma R')
key_items.statement: P ⪰ 0 Hermitian with rank P ≤ r; Q Hermitian with n₊(Q) ≤ b; then ∀c > 0: c·tr P − (c²/4)r + 2c·tr Q − c²b ≤ ‖P+Q‖²_F; at c=2: r ≥ 2 tr P + 4 tr Q − 4b − ‖P+Q‖²_F. Proof: Jordan-decompose Q, drop tr(PQ₊) ≥ 0, von Neumann on tr(PQ₋) with 2μν ≤ 2cν + ν² + (μ−c)²₊, Cauchy–Schwarz on ≤ b positive eigenvalues, g_c(μ) ≥ cμ − c²/4. It is 'Montgomery's integer step m² ≥ 2m−1 transplanted to real eigenvalues, where it holds for free.' Tightness against this information: lemmaR_tight (2c·tr(P+Q) − ‖P+Q‖²_F = Σ_j k_c(m_j) + c²b at the extremal configurations).

key_items.name: The final certificate and constants (Theorems A–C)
key_items.statement: n^dist_on(I′) ≥ 4 tr A − 2N(I′) − ‖A‖²_F ≥ (H(λ) − o(1))N, H(λ) = 2 − 1/λ − λ/3, using only: |u_i|² ≤ 1 (Poisson identity, dropping nonnegative terms), rank M_on ≤ n^dist_on, n₊(M_p) ≤ n^dist_pair, N(I′) ≥ N_on + 2n_pair, tail ‖E‖ ≤ 2A₀L²log(4T)T^{λ/2−1}. Theorem A: liminf N₀*/N ≥ 2/3; B: 2/3 simple-and-on-line (via regrouping: 3s₁ + 4s₂ + 4p ≥ 4tr − ‖·‖²_F, the m² ≥ 3m−2 analogue); C: 5/6 distinct. Sharp for {tr, ‖·‖²_F, block structure}: extremal = (2N/3) lattice simples + (N/6) tight pairs, spectrally Montgomery's RH-extremal.

key_items.name: Theorem D (optimal window = Montgomery–Taylor exactly)
key_items.statement: Maximizing c_λ(v) = λ(∫v)²/(∫v² + λ²∬|s−s′|v(s)v(s′)) over v ≥ 0 gives v*(s) = cos(√2 λs), c₁* = √2 tan θ/(1 + θ tan θ), θ = 1/√2; c₁* = 0.7532961, 1/c₁* = 1/2 + 2^{−1/2}cot(2^{−1/2}) = 1.3274992 (Montgomery–Taylor constant). Results: 2 − 1/c₁* = 0.67250 (on-line and simple), (3 − 1/c₁*)/2 = 0.83625 (distinct). By CCLM17 Cor. 14 this is 'the limit of the method block structure + two traces + primes up to T: no window does better' given F on [−1,1] only; positivity constraint v ≥ 0 is inactive.

key_items.name: Proposition 7.4 (the Cap) + λ ≤ 1 wall
key_items.statement: For any window and θ ≥ 0: rank P₁ ≤ rank P ≤ d and n₊^θ(G̃) ≤ d = λ₁N + O(1); no argument based on Prop 4.1 with support L = λl certifies more than λ₁N on-line points; the certificate is ≤ (2 − 1/λ₁ + o(1))N, non-positive for λ ≤ 1/2. λ ≤ 1 forced by Prop 5.6: for X ≫ Tl the off-diagonal requires Hardy–Littlewood/PCC-for-α>1 information. 'Nothing in the method distinguishes between two thirds and all.'

key_items.name: Higher-moments no-go
key_items.statement: tr G̃^k is diagonal-evaluable exactly in the Rudnick–Sarnak range kλ < 2. k=3: admissible for λ < 2/3, but an odd moment cannot improve a count on [0,∞) — mass ε at height h → ∞ feeds m₃ freely; LP-dual: any certificate c₁μ + c₂μ² + c₃μ³ ≤ 1 on (0,∞) needs c₃ ≤ 0. Would help only with λ_max(G̃) = O(1), i.e. sup of Σ_{n≤X}Λ(n)n^{−1/2−iτ} on windows of length 1/L — Lindelöf-strength, unavailable. k=4: needs λ < 1/2 where d < N/2 kills everything. General no-go = 'Theorem U' (E2-HL agent).

key_items.name: Bandwidth-one ceiling (formalized)
key_items.statement: Stability: for any certificate (c₀, r), r ∈ C¹[0,1], r′ differentiable off a countable set, valid against a form-factor configuration with grid masses s_j and simple-point fraction p: c₀ + ∫₀¹ r(x)x dx ≤ p + |r(1)||D(1)| + |r′(1)||E(1)| + (sup|E|)∫₀¹|r″|. Instantiated at an explicit 256-periodic law (near-CUE rows |256·S(j) − j| ≤ 3·10⁻⁴⁰ for 0<j<256, |D(1)| ≤ 0.82395317, checked by kernel `decide`): every bandwidth-one certificate certifies simple-zero proportion ≤ 0.6818287 + 2.55·10⁻⁶·(|r′(1)| + ∫|r″|); law's exact p₀ = 10909258999421303588095230195816054408197/16·10³⁹ = 0.68182868746. Sole hypothesis: EnclOK (enclosures from exact-rational certificate, sha256 cc3de9917db4d14d...). Paper form: 'no certificate of this kind... can certify a proportion of simple zeros exceeding 0.68185'; 2/3 is within 0.016 of its own method's ceiling; 0.70/0.80/0.90 need support ≈ 1.04/1.26/1.70.
