key_items.name: Failed per-pair pricing (why the lemma must be mass-linear)
key_items.statement: Normalized experiment (v^Tv = 1): min ‖M‖²_F = n_on + 4n_p exactly (13 cases, 5 decimals) — integrality survives interactions. But all free variants fail: G2/G1 gap = −4.000 (free phase: v = e^{−iπ/4}r makes 2Re(vv^T) = 0 while charged 4); G3 gap −0.5/−1.333 (negative-Re s pairs priced 0 but subtract); phase-locked G4 gap −0.25…−0.73 (degenerate pairs s → 0, A ~ 10³–10⁵ act as free mass movers). Conclusion: normalization did two jobs (phase + mass quantization); correct inequality is linear in masses like Σm² ≥ Σ(2m−1). Pair–pair cross terms can be ~ −4A²: deep pairs offset by half a grid cell nearly cancel ('quadrupoles'), so termwise diagonal dominance is FALSE — same phenomenon that forced BGSTB to assume |β − 1/2| < 1/(2 log T).

key_items.name: Simplicity limitation and the two levels of integrality
key_items.statement: Direct rank route gives only N₀^simple ≥ 2n^dist_on − N_on ≥ (3 − 2t)N = N/3 at λ=1. The (m−1)(m−2) ≥ 0 spectral level is destroyed by interactions: eigenvalues of interacting simple zeros fill (0,2), and 'no eigenvalue in (1,2)' is false already under RH+GUE (Gram spectrum mean 1, variance 1/3 at λ=1). Paper's repair: regrouping (P₁, Q′) — multiple on-line points and off-line pairs all moved to the index side at flat charge 4 — recovers (m−1)(m−2) ≥ 0 and gives Theorem B's 2/3 simple; this is CGG98 (1.2) 'made unconditional.'

key_items.name: Theorem E and the degree obstruction
key_items.statement: For fixed primitive χ mod q: same 2/3, 2/3, 5/6 and Theorem D analogues (proof changes only: ν_{X,χ} density, no pole term, |χ(n)|²=1 leaves diagonal unchanged). Hybrid range (heuristic): q ≤ T^θ gives H(1/(1+θ)), positive for θ < √6/3. General degree m_F: c = Λ/(1 + m_F Λ²/3) with Λ < Λ* = lim log T/log q(T); always c ≤ Λ*, so non-vacuous only if Λ* > 3−√6; GL(2) individually: c = 6/13 < 1/2 — nothing. Family averaging restores Λ* = 1 (expected averaged 2/3 for q → ∞, T ~ power of log q; needs Gevrey taper; not carried out). Davenport–Heilbronn: Prop 5.6 fails, certificate empty.

key_items.name: Conditional ladder and RH-unreachability
key_items.statement: HL*(k₀,λ): tr G̃^k = dℓ₁^k(m_k(λ) + o(1)) with sine-kernel moments m_k(1) = 1, 4/3, 2, 13/4 (k ≤ 4). HL*(4,λ) ∀λ<1 ⇒ liminf N₀^s/N ≥ 13/18 (via Christoffel function Λ₂(0;1) = 5/36); HL*(k,λ) ∀k,λ<1 ⇒ proportion 1 of simple on-line zeros — 'the ceiling of Prop 7.4; RH itself is out of reach of the mechanism.' Complementary: GLSS25 (PCC full support ⇒ 100% simple). Under RH the third trace is a theorem and cubic weights ψ(m) = m/2 + (2m²−m³)/18 + (4/9)1_{m=1} give N_d ≥ 0.85082 (vs. 0.8477 CGdL).

result.summary:
This artifact is a complete, sorry-free Lean 4/Mathlib formalization (toolchain v4.33.0-rc2) of "More than two thirds of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie on the critical line" (Anthropic, 2026): Theorems A-E plus two extras (zeros of ξ′; a formalized no-go "bandwidth-one ceiling"). Top-level theorems are hypothesis-free (#print axioms = the 3 standard Lean axioms). The architecture is: (1) an abstract layer `ZeroConfig` (Zeta23/Defs.lean) — any locally finite multiset in the strip invariant under ρ ↦ 1−ρ̄ — so the entire zero-side is arithmetic-free; (2) a Prop-structure `PaperInputs` (Zeta23/Hypotheses.lean) bundling exactly five classical inputs (Weil EF in the paper's spectral normalization, Riemann-von Mangoldt + local count N(t+1)−N(t) ≤ A₀log(t+3), Chebyshev-Mertens, Montgomery-Vaughan weighted Hilbert, Stirling facts for μ = Γ-density), every one of which is then PROVED from Mathlib (contour integration at Re s = 5/4 with pigeonholed good heights, Landau/Borel-Caratheodory partial fractions, a from-scratch MV proof via the Preissmann-Lévêque eigen-identity with constant 13, etc.); (3) the method: a Gabor system f_k(u) = φ(u)e^{−iτ_k u} on the grid τ_k = T + 2πk/L, k < d ≈ LT/2π, with taper φ supported exactly in [−L/2, L/2], L = λ·log(T/2π), X = e^L = (T/2π)^λ. The Gram matrix G_{kl} = W(f_k,f_l) has a zero-side expression Σ_ρ m_ρ φ̂(γ_ρ−τ_k)φ̂(γ_ρ−τ_l) and a prime-side expression ∫ φ̂(τ−τ_k)φ̂(τ−τ_l)ν_X(τ)dτ, ν_X = μ + Π_X + P_X. Zero side: block decomposition Â = P + Q (P ⪰ 0 from on-line atoms, rank P ≤ s₁+s₂, tr P ≤ N_on via the Gabor-Poisson identity Σ_k φ̂(γ−τ_k)² = aL²; n₊(Q) ≤ p off-line pairs via Sylvester inertia), a tail bound ‖Ẽ‖ ≤ θ₀ ≪ l·T^{λ/2−1}, and the rank-trace inequality c·trP − (c²/4)r + 2c·trQ − c²b ≤ ‖P+Q‖_F² (proved via von Neumann's trace inequality). Prime side: tr G̃ = aLN(1+O(ℰ_T)) and tr G̃² = 2πbL∫_T^{2T}μ² + (T/π)Σ_{n≤X}Λ(n)²n⁻¹g(log n) + O(cross terms), where g = φ²⋆φ² and the off-diagonal prime-pair term is bounded by MV as 16·C_MV·(∫Φ²)·Σ_{n≤X}Λ(n)² = O(L²X) with NO cancellation. The certificate (Assembly/Certificate.lean): if tr Ĝ ≥ (1−δ)N and ‖Ĝ‖_F² ≤ (κ+δ)N then N₀* ≥ (2−κ−ε)N; flat window κ = 1/λ₁ + λ₁/3 gives 2/3 at λ = 1; the window-general ratio is cRatio = λ₁a²/(b+λ₁²J), maximized by the Montgomery-Taylor profile v*_λ(s) = cos(√2λs) with closed form c*_λ = √2 tanϑ/(1+ϑ tanϑ), ϑ = λ/√2, giving Theorem D's 2 − 1/c₁* = 0.67250… (all via a clean one-variable variational file ThmD/Functional.lean and a λ → 1⁻ continuity passage).

The most research-relevant component is the formalized obstruction (Zeta23/PairCeiling/): a stability inequality proved by two integrations by parts against the integrated pair-correlation discrepancy shows that ANY certificate (c₀, r) of the Theorem-B type that is valid against a configuration whose form-factor measure is the explicit 256-periodic near-CUE law certifies a simple-zero proportion of at most 0.6818287 + 2.5431316·10⁻⁶·(|r′(1)| + ∫|r″|). The law's 255 row inequalities |256·S(j) − j| ≤ 3·10⁻⁴⁰ and edge bound |D(1)| ≤ 0.82395317 are kernel-checked by `decide` from 256 integer enclosures (the one hypothesis, EnclOK, produced outside Lean by interval arithmetic from an exact-rational certificate with recorded sha256). So the formalization contains, machine-checked, both the achievement (0.6725) and the near-matching ceiling (0.68183) of the entire bandwidth-one Levinson/pair-correlation paradigm: the gap between what this method gives and what it can ever give is ~0.009, and going further provably requires either arithmetic input beyond Chebyshev+MV (prime pair correlations, i.e. test-function bandwidth > 1) or spectral quantities beyond {trace, Frobenius norm, rank, positive index} of the Gram matrix (the tightness theorem lemmaR_tight closes the purely linear-algebraic escape route).

Also formalized: the same machinery for primitive Dirichlet L-functions (Theorem E, fixed modulus q > 1) and for ξ′ (Farmer-Gonek-Lee transfer; 0.85838 simple-on-line / 0.92919 distinct with the flat window, 0.86864/0.93432 with a quartic window), demonstrating that the whole pipeline (EF, Gabor grid, rank-trace certificate, prime-side traces) is genuinely modular and re-instantiable for other L-functions and derivatives.

key_items.statement: For every L > 0 and f,g : ℝ → ℂ with ContDiff ℝ 2 and tsupport ⊆ Icc(−L/2, L/2): (i) Σ_ρ m_ρ h_f(γ_ρ)·conj(h_g(conj γ_ρ)) is Summable; (ii) τ ↦ h_f(τ)conj(h_g(τ))ν_X(τ) is Integrable; (iii) W(f,g) = ∫_ℝ h_f(τ)conj(h_g(τ))ν_X(τ)dτ, X = e^L, where h_f(z) = ∫f(u)e^{izu}du (paperFT; = 𝓕f(−τ/2π)), γ_ρ = (ρ−1/2)/i, and ν_X = μ + Π_X + P_X with μ(τ) = (1/2π)Re ψ(1/4+iτ/2) − logπ/2π, Π_X(τ) = 1/(2π(1/4+τ²)) + (1/π)Re((X^s−1)/s), s = 1/2+iτ, P_X(τ) = −(1/π)Σ_{n≤X}Λ(n)n^{−1/2}cos(τ log n). key_items.name: H-MV: Montgomery-Vaughan weighted Hilbert inequality, as proved
key_items.statement: MVDiag 13: for any finite family of distinct reals freq with admissible weights (0 < δ_r ≤ |freq r − freq s| ∀ s ≠ r), |Σ_{r≠s} x_r conj(x_s)/(freq r − freq s)| ≤ 13·Σ_r|x_r|²/δ_r. Proof: skew kernel k_{rs} = √δ_r√δ_s/(freq r−freq s), M = iK Hermitian; Preissmann-Lévêque eigen-identity (arXiv:2203.14950 Lem 2.1) gives μ²·|u_m|² = Σ(c_mc_n)²|u_n|²/(Δ)² + 2Σc_m³c_n Re(u_m ū_n)/(Δ)²; summing with spacing_sq (Σ_{t≠s}δ_t/(freq s−freq t)² ≤ 9/δ_s) and Uform_le (≤ 73) yields μ² ≤ 9 + 2·73 = 155 ≤ 13². Also proved: spacing_four (≤ 27/δ³) and a two_point lemma (≤ 36(δ_ℓ+δ_m)/(δ_ℓδ_m(freq ℓ−freq m)²)).

key_items.name: Gabor-Poisson identity [lem:poisson]
key_items.statement: For φ continuous, even, φ(u) = 0 for |u| ≥ L/2, with sup_s |φ̂(s)|(1+s²) < ∞: for all T,τ,τ′, Σ_{k∈ℤ} φ̂(τ−τ_k)φ̂(τ′−τ_k) = L·(φ²)^(τ−τ′) with τ_k = T + 2πk/L; in particular Σ_k φ̂(γ−τ_k)² = aL², a = L⁻¹∫φ². This is what makes tr P computable on the zero side (each on-line zero contributes exactly aL² across the full grid) and is window-agnostic and grid-translation-invariant.

key_items.name: Rank-trace inequality + tightness (the linear-algebra engine)
key_items.statement: For P ⪰ 0 with rank P ≤ r, Q Hermitian with n₊(Q) ≤ b, c > 0: c·trP − (c²/4)r + 2c·trQ − c²b ≤ ‖P+Q‖_F² (proof: positive/negative parts of Q, von Neumann trace inequality, two scalar estimates). c = 2 form: r ≥ 2trP + 4trQ − 4b − ‖P+Q‖_F². TIGHTNESS (lemmaR_tight): for on-line atoms with integer multiplicities m_j ≤ c on orthonormal vectors plus b pair-blocks of eigenvalue c, 2c·tr(P+Q) − ‖P+Q‖_F² = Σ_j k_c(m_j) + c²b — the certificate cannot be improved using only these spectral quantities.

Cross terms: 𝓜[μ,P_X] ≪ l√X, 𝓜[μ,Π_X] ≪ lL√X, 𝓜[P_X,Π_X] ≪ LX, 𝓜[Π_X,Π_X] ≪ LX/T. key_items.statement: cFun λ v := λ(∫_{−1/2}^{1/2}v)² / (∫v² + λ²∬|s−s′|v(s)v(s′)dsds′); optimizer v*_λ(s) = cos(√2·λ·s); cFun λ v*_λ = cStar λ := √2 sinϑ/(cosϑ + ϑ sinϑ) = √2 tanϑ/(1+ϑtanϑ), ϑ = λ/√2 (proved: cFun_vStar, via a* = √2 sinϑ/λ, b* = 1/2 + sin2ϑ/4ϑ, J* = sin2ϑ/8ϑ³ − cos2ϑ/4ϑ²; b* + λ²J* = a*(cosϑ + ϑsinϑ)). Window-general ratio cRatio λ₁ a b J = λ₁a²/(b+λ₁²J); concrete window φ_D(u) = √(v*_λ(u/L))·φ_flat(u). Constants: c₁* = cStar 1 = 0.75329…; HD(1) = 2 − 1/c₁* = 3/2 − (1/√2)cot(1/√2) = 0.67250…; N₀ˢ rate 2c₁*−1 = 0.50659 (CS form), 2−1/c₁* (rank-trace mult form); N_d rate (3−1/c₁*)/2 = 0.83625. result.bandwidth_role: The bandwidth is λ = P.lam with L = λ·log(T/2π), X = e^L = (T/2π)^λ; the constraint is the field lam_le_one : P.lam ≤ 1 in Params.Valid (Defs.lean:196) and in every prime-side Facts structure (PrimeSideB.lean:359, ThmD/Traces.lean:39, ThmE/TracesChi.lean:77). It enters through three distinct mechanisms. (1) SUPPORT OF TEST FUNCTIONS: the explicit formula requires tsupport f,g ⊆ [−L/2, L/2], so the Weil test k = f⋆g̃ has support in [−L,L] and the prime side sees only prime powers n ≤ X = e^L (prime_summand_eq_zero, ExplicitFormula.lean:315) — the Dirichlet-polynomial length is exactly e^L. (2) WHERE λ ≤ 1 BITES ANALYTICALLY: the binding error is the off-diagonal prime-pair term 𝒪₁ of 𝓜[P_X,P_X], bounded via MV with min-gap weights δ_n = 1/(2n) by 16·C_MV·(∫Φ²)·Σ_{n≤X}Λ(n)² ≈ L·(X·L) = L²X (PPOffDiag.lean:40) — pure absolute values, zero cancellation extracted from Σ_{n≠m}Λ(n)Λ(m)/√(nm)·kernel(log n − log m). This must be o of the main term (TL/2π)(ℓ₁²+L²/3) ≈ Tl³; at λ = 1, L²X = l²·T/2π and the ratio is 1/l → 0 (barely); for any λ > 1, L²X = l²T^λ ≫ Tl³ and the whole second-moment computation collapses. Concretely the regime lemma requires X ≤ T (eventually_X_le_T, used at PrimeSideB.lean:479) and ℰ_T = w/L + (l²+X)log l/(Tl) + T^{λ/2−1} → 0 (calE_tendsto_zero needs lam_le_one, Main.lean:149) — the middle term diverges for λ > 1. No single lemma 'fails at the boundary' λ = 1 itself (the certificate takes λ → 1⁻ by continuity of cStar, cStar_continuousOn); the failure for λ > 1 is that the MV bound on 𝒪₁ and the ends/cross bounds are no longer o(main term). (3) THE CEILING: PairCeiling formalizes that this is not an artifact of the error analysis — the entire information content available at bandwidth ≤ 1 (equivalently, pair-correlation form factor known only on [−1,1]) caps every certificate of this shape at ≃ 0.68183 simple-zero proportion, 0.009 above the achieved 0.6725. The variational file quantifies the value of more bandwidth: cStar λ is increasing (2 − 1/c*_λ would reach 3/4 near λ ≈ 1.706 and → 1 only as λ → ∞), so every unit of bandwidth beyond 1 has an explicit payoff; obtaining it requires genuine prime-correlation input.
limitations: Formalized ceiling (PairCeiling): no certificate (c₀, r) of the Theorem-B/rank-trace type with bandwidth-one data — r ∈ C¹[0,1], r′ of bounded variation — valid against all admissible configurations can certify a simple-zero proportion above 0.6818287 + 2.55·10⁻⁶·(|r′(1)| + ∫|r″|); the obstruction is an explicit adversarial 256-periodic near-CUE form-factor law, kernel-checked. The method therefore provably cannot approach proportion 1 (RH-strength) without leaving the bandwidth-one certificate class.

The zero side 'contains no arithmetic' (paper §4, formalized as ZeroConfig): all zero-side inequalities hold for arbitrary reflection-invariant locally finite multisets with N(t+1)−N(t) ≪ log t. This is a strength (modularity) and a fundamental weakness: any conclusion derivable in this framework must also hold for the adversarial law, so RH itself is out of reach of the abstract layer by construction; new arithmetic must enter through the PaperInputs boundary.

Off-diagonal prime pairs are bounded in absolute value via MV (δ_n = 1/(2n)); pushing the polynomial length past X = T (λ > 1) would require asymptotics for shifted convolutions Σ Λ(n)Λ(n+h) (Hardy–Littlewood/additive divisor), which are unproven — this is the classical wall, and the formalization localizes it to exactly one lemma-chain (O1_bound → prop_PP → tr2).

Lemma R is proved TIGHT (lemmaR_tight, ZeroSide/TightMult.lean): using only tr(P+Q), ‖P+Q‖_F², rank bounds and n₊ bounds, the rank-trace certificate cannot be improved. Escaping requires new spectral functionals of the Gram matrix (e.g. tr Ĝ³ / eigenvalue-distribution information), for which no prime-side evaluation exists at bandwidth 1 beyond the second moment.

The explicit formula is formalized ONLY for C_c² test functions with support ⊆ [−L/2, L/2] (compact support is load-bearing: prime sum finite, EL truncation in the pole term). Gaussians, Schwartz functions, or the test functions of Li-coefficient/Weil-positivity computations with noncompact support are outside the proved class and would need a new limiting argument with tail control on the zero sum (ZeroSummability gives absolute convergence only via (1+|r|)^{-2} decay from compact support + C²).

Results are proportional and dyadic (windows (T,2T], liminf ε-form): no information about individual zeros, no zero-density estimates off the line, no bound of the form N(T) − N₀(T) = o(N(T)); off-line zeros are only counted, never excluded.
Theorem E is for FIXED primitive χ mod q > 1 (constants and T₀ depend on q; no q-uniformity is claimed), so no application to q-aspect problems as formalized.

Deviation from the paper (documented, PrimeSideA.lean header): error constants C and thresholds T₀ may depend on λ (fixed-λ reading, sufficient because the endpoint is taken by λ → 1⁻ continuity); the paper's uniform-in-λ constants are not formalized.

MV is proved with constant 13 (diagonal) / 26 (bilinear), not the optimal 3π/2 — harmless here (∃C form), but any application where the MV constant is load-bearing (e.g. explicit density estimates) would need the sharper constant.

The variational optimality of v*_λ (that cStar λ = sup_v cFun λ v) is NOT formalized — only cFun λ v*_λ = cStar λ. The upper-bound half of the Montgomery–Taylor problem lives in the paper/PairCeiling, not in ThmD.
extension_hooks: ZeroConfig + PaperInputs seam (Defs.lean, Hypotheses.lean): the cleanest plug-in point for new mathematics. Any new arithmetic input (e.g. a proven correlation estimate for Λ, a sixth-moment bound, a zero-density theorem) can be added as a new Prop field and consumed by the abstract assembly; conversely any theorem about abstract reflection-invariant configurations proved elsewhere instantiates immediately at ζ, Dirichlet L, ξ′ via the existing seams (zetaZeros, ThmE, XiPrime).

The EF machinery (WeilEF/: rectangle contour, good-heights pigeonhole, Landau partial fractions, ZeroSummability, plus the normalization chain ExplicitFormula.lean) is a reusable template for Weil-type explicit formulas of any completed L-function with a functional equation — already re-instantiated twice (Dirichlet, ξ′/ξ). Extending EF_lit from C_c² to a weighted/Schwartz class (adding a tail-control lemma to ZeroSummability) is the concrete prerequisite for formalizing Weil's positivity criterion or Li coefficients on this codebase; W(f,f) and the ν_X-integral identity are already defined and proved equal for compact support.

Pair correlation with larger support: the prime-side pipeline (Mform bilinear expansion, shear+Fubini in PP.lean, the 8-term MV decomposition in PPKernel/PPOffDiag) is exactly Montgomery's F(α) computation for |α| ≤ 1. A proven shifted-convolution input would replace O1_bound by a main term; the file boundaries (O1_bound → prop_PP field of Facts → tr2) make the required interface explicit: one EvBound field with X > T. The λ-dependence is otherwise generic — FactsD keeps λ symbolic throughout.

The variational layer (ThmD/Functional.lean, cRatio = λ₁a²/(b+λ₁²J), window-general FactsD): any new window enters through three moments (a, b, J); supports experimenting with other profiles (the quartic XiPrime window already demonstrates this), multi-parameter or complex-modulated windows. A genuinely two-variable certificate (using off-diagonal Gram data beyond ‖Ĝ‖_F²) would need a new functional here plus a new prime-side trace — the tightness theorem says this is the ONLY way forward within bandwidth 1.

LinAlg/RankTrace + TightMult: the Hermitian-matrix certificate layer (von Neumann, Sylvester inertia both directions, Weyl, posIndex calculus) is self-contained (namespace RHLinalg) and could host stronger certificates: higher-moment inequalities (tr Ĝ³), interlacing/majorization arguments, or block-resolved versions; lemmaR_tight precisely characterizes what invariants are exhausted.

PairCeiling/Stability.lean is a general-purpose tool for proving ceilings: for ANY proposed new certificate family, instantiating ceiling_stability against candidate adversarial laws gives a machine-checked upper bound on what the family can certify — a negative-space search instrument for method design. The EnclOK/decide/RowCert infrastructure (integer enclosures + kernel verification, external certificate with recorded sha256) is a reusable pattern for importing interval-arithmetic computations into Lean proofs.

The Gabor-Poisson lemma (Poisson.lean) is proved for arbitrary continuous even compactly supported windows with quadratic Fourier decay and arbitrary grid offset T: supports multi-grid systems, refined grids (h = 2π/L is what makes the frame tight — changing the density trades tr P against rank bounds), or vector-valued/多window Gabor frames, none of which are used by the paper.

MV/Spacing.lean already contains stronger unexploited lemmas (spacing_four σ=4, two_point) sufficient for third/fourth-moment off-diagonal analyses; the Preissmann–Lévêque eigen-identity route would formalize sharper MV constants (3π/2 or Preissmann's) if ever load-bearing.

XiPrime/ demonstrates the transfer-to-derivative pattern (Farmer–Gonek–Lee): the same rank-trace device applied to ξ^{(k)} for higher k, or to other differentiations/convolutions of ξ, is a mechanical extension; the coefficient-system files (XiPrime/Transfer) show how to re-derive the needed EF variant.

Theorem E's fixed-q formalization invites a q-uniform version (constants tracked in q): the EvBound/EventuallyAt error discipline used throughout makes the T-dependence explicit already; repeating it for q would formalize proportions on the critical line uniformly in conductor — relevant to Levinson-type results for families.

result.summary:
This artifact (paper "More than two thirds of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie on the critical line", Claude/Anthropic 2026, + a sorry-free Lean 4/Mathlib formalization, /Users/jaytyagi/Documents/Work/2026/Math/riemann/anthropic/zeta-23-lean-main) makes Montgomery's 1973 RH-conditional pair-correlation argument unconditional by replacing the RH-dependent "termwise positivity of the zero side" with finite-dimensional linear algebra. The pipeline: (1) Weil's explicit formula is read as a Hermitian form W(f,g) = Σ_ρ m_ρ f̂(γ_ρ)ĝ(γ_ρ) on C²_c test functions, whose positivity on all of C²_c is equivalent to RH (Weil/Bombieri); here γ_ρ = (ρ−1/2)/i is complex off the line, |Im γ_ρ| < 1/2. (2) W is compressed to a Gabor family V = span{f_k = φ(u)e^{−iτ_k u}}, τ_k = T + 2πk/L, k < d = ⌊LT/2π⌋, with a C³ taper φ supported on [−L/2, L/2], L = λ log(T/2π), λ ≤ 1; the resulting d×d real-symmetric Gram matrix G_kl = W(f_k,f_l) has an aliasing-free Poisson sampling identity Σ_{k∈Z} φ̂(τ−τ_k)φ̂(τ′−τ_k) = LΦ(τ−τ′), Φ = (φ²)^. In the units Ĝ = G/(aL²), a = L⁻¹∫φ², an isolated on-line zero contributes eigenvalue exactly m_ρ. (3) Zero side (§4): by the functional-equation symmetry ρ ↦ 1−ρ̄, Ĝ = P + Q + (tail): each distinct on-line point gives a rank-one PSD atom (rank P ≤ s₁+s₂, tr P ≤ N_on by the sampling identity), each off-line pair {ρ, 1−ρ̄} a signature-(1,1) hyperbolic block, so n₊(Q) ≤ p by Sylvester inertia pull-back (Lemma 3.1, needing no independence of the evaluation functionals). Far zeros are a perturbation of operator/trace norm θ₀ ≪ l·T^{λ/2−1} (Prop 4.2; requires the taper — sharp cutoff fails). (4) Linear algebra (§3, "Lemma R"): for P ⪰ 0, rank P ≤ r, n₊(Q) ≤ b, ‖P+Q‖²_F ≥ c·tr P − (c²/4)r + 2c·tr Q − c²b for all c > 0 (von Neumann trace inequality); c = 2 is the matrix transplant of m² ≥ 2m−1, and the regrouping "simple zeros on the rank side / multiples+pairs on the index side" (Prop 4.4) transplants m² ≥ 3m−2, giving 3s₁+4s₂+4p ≥ 4 tr Â − ‖Â‖²_F. (5) Prime side (§5): tr Ĝ and ‖Ĝ‖²_F are Montgomery's first and second moments, evaluated UNCONDITIONALLY (this is [BGSTB24]'s observation, redone with full error terms): tr Ĝ = N(1+o(1)) and ‖Ĝ‖²_F = (1/λ₁ + λ₁/3)N(1+O(E_T)), the λ₁/3 coming from the prime-diagonal Σ Λ(n)²/n g(log n) = L³J/2 + O(L²) and the off-diagonal Σ_{n≠m} being ≪ L²X = o(main) via the Montgomery–Vaughan generalized Hilbert inequality. Combining: s₁ ≥ (2 − 1/λ − λ/3 − o(1))N = (H(λ)−o(1))N, so at λ=1 at least 2/3 of zeros (with multiplicity) are simple AND on the line (Theorems A, B), and N_d ≥ ((1+H)/2 − o(1))N = 5/6·N (Theorem C).

Theorem D optimizes the window: writing φ²(u) = v(u/L), the certified proportion 2 − 1/c is governed by the scale-free functional c_λ(v) = λ(∫v)²/(∫v² + λ²∬|s−s′|v(s)v(s′)) on [−1/2,1/2]; its Euler–Lagrange equation v + λ²Tv = const (T the |s−s′| kernel) i.e. v″ + 2λ²v = 0 has optimizer v*_λ(s) = cos(√2 λs) > 0 (constraint v ≥ 0 inactive), with c*_λ = √2 tan ϑ/(1 + ϑ tan ϑ), ϑ = λ/√2. At λ=1, c₁* = 0.7532960678…, 1/c₁* = 1/2 + 2^{−1/2}cot(2^{−1/2}) = 1.3274992963… (the Montgomery–Taylor constant), giving lim inf N₀*/N ≥ 2 − 1/c₁* = 0.6725007…, same for simple-on-line, and N_d/N ≥ (3 − 1/c₁*)/2 = 0.8362503…. By [CCLM17, Cor. 14] this kernel solves the one-delta extremal problem for F restricted to [−1,1], so Theorem D is the exact limit of "block structure + two traces + primes up to T". Theorem E extends everything to primitive Dirichlet L-functions (fixed q); a ξ′ variant gives 0.85838 (flat) / 0.86864 (quartic window 1 − (7/100)(2s)² − (51/200)(2s)⁴) simple-on-line for zeros of ξ′, de-conditionalizing Farmer–Gonek–Lee.

The formalization adds two research-grade artifacts beyond A–E. (i) Tightness of Lemma R (Zeta23/ZeroSide/TightMult.lean): on configurations "on-line atoms with integer multiplicities m_j ≤ c on orthonormal vectors ⊕ b pair-blocks of eigenvalue c", 2c·tr(P+Q) − ‖P+Q‖²_F = Σ_j k_c(m_j) + c²b exactly (k_c(p) = c² − ((c−p)₊)²), so the certificate provably CANNOT separate an on-line double zero from an off-line pair of depth → 0, and cannot be improved using only (tr, ‖·‖²_F, integer atoms, n₊). (ii) The bandwidth-one ceiling (Zeta23/PairCeiling/): a "certificate" is abstracted as a pair (c₀, r), r ∈ C¹[0,1] with r″ integrable, certifying simple-zero fraction v = c₀ + ∫₀¹ r(x)x dx, "valid" against a configuration with form-factor grid masses s_j at j/N and simple-point fraction p₁ iff c₀ + Σ_j s_j r(j/N) ≤ p₁. Two integrations by parts give the stability bound v ≤ p₁ + |r(1)||D(1)| + |r′(1)||E(1)| + (sup|E|)∫₀¹|r″| where D(x) = C(x) − x²/2, E = ∫₀ˣD. Instantiated at an explicit 256-periodic extremal law (exact-rational LP over marked configurations, marks m ∈ {1,2}, form factor S(j) = j/256 up to τ = 3·10⁻⁴⁰, |D(1)| ≤ 0.82395317, simple fraction p₀ = 0.68182868746… exactly rational): every bandwidth-one certificate with r(1) = 0 certifies at most 0.6818287 + 2.5431316·10⁻⁶·(|r′(1)| + ∫|r″|). Theorem B's 2/3 is thus within 0.0152 of its own method's ceiling; the paper states that pushing to 0.70/0.80/0.90 would need pair-correlation support out to ≈1.04/1.26/1.70.

key_items.name: Weil form + spectral explicit formula (Prop 2.1)
key_items.statement: W(f,g) = Σ_ρ m_ρ f̂(γ_ρ)ĝ(γ_ρ) with γ_ρ = (ρ−1/2)/i; for supp f, supp g ⊆ [−L/2, L/2]: W(f,g) = ∫_R f̂(τ)ĝ(τ)ν_X(τ)dτ, ν_X = µ + Π_X + P_X, µ = (2π)⁻¹Re Γ′/Γ(1/4+iτ/2) − log π/2π, P_X = −π⁻¹Σ_{n≤X}Λ(n)n^{−1/2}cos(τ log n), X = e^L. Positivity of W on all C²_c ⟺ RH.

key_items.name: Gabor compression + critical-density sampling (Lemma 2.2)
key_items.statement: V = span{φ(u)e^{−iτ_k u}}, τ_k = T + kh, h = 2π/L, d = ⌊LT/2π⌋ ≈ λ₁N; Σ_{k∈Z} φ̂(τ−τ_k)φ̂(τ′−τ_k) = LΦ(τ−τ′) exactly (Φ = (φ²)^), because supp φ + supp φ ⊆ [−L, L] kills all nonzero Poisson modes. In units Ĝ = G/(aL²) an isolated on-line zero has eigenvalue exactly m_ρ.

key_items.name: Zero-side block structure (Prop 4.1)
key_items.statement: Â = P + Q: P ⪰ 0 from on-line points (rank P ≤ s₁+s₂, tr P ≤ N_on via sampling identity), each off-line pair {ρ,1−ρ̄} a 2×2 block [[0,m_ρ],[m_ρ,0]] of signature (1,1); n₊(Q) ≤ p by inertia pull-back (Lemma 3.1 — no independence of evaluation functionals needed, indifferent to depth |β−1/2|).

key_items.name: Rank–trace inequality (Lemma 3.2 = 'Lemma R')
key_items.statement: P ⪰ 0, rank P ≤ r, n₊(Q) ≤ b ⇒ ∀c>0: ‖P+Q‖²_F ≥ c·tr P − (c²/4)r + 2c·tr Q − c²b (via von Neumann trace inequality tr(PQ₋) ≤ Σp_i n_i). c=2 ⇒ r ≥ 2tr P + 4tr Q − 4b − ‖P+Q‖²_F, matrix analogue of m² ≥ 2m−1; regrouped (P₁ = simple atoms, Q′ = multiples+pairs) it is m² ≥ 3m−2: 3s₁+4s₂+4p ≥ 4tr Â − ‖Â‖²_F (Prop 4.4(i)). Not scale-invariant — must be applied in units Ĝ = G/(aL²).

key_items.name: Multiplicity-aware Lemma R and its TIGHTNESS
key_items.statement: k-form: 2c·tr(P+Q) − ‖P+Q‖²_F ≤ Σ_j k_c(m_j‖v_j‖²) + c²b, k_c(p) = c² − ((c−p)₊)². TIGHT: for on-line atoms with integer m_j ≤ c on orthonormal vectors plus b pair-blocks of eigenvalue c, equality holds exactly — the certificate cannot distinguish an on-line double (m=2, k₂=4) from an off-line tight pair (charge c²=4), and no further inequality in (tr, ‖·‖²_F, n₊, integer atoms) can improve it.

key_items.name: Tail estimate (Prop 4.2) — where the taper is forced
key_items.statement: ‖Ẽ‖ ≤ θ₀ = 4A₀C₁²X^{1/2}log(4T)/D₀², C₁ = ‖φ″‖₁, D₀ = T^{1/2}, so θ₀ ≪ l·T^{λ/2−1}; the X^{1/2} = e^{L·sup|Im γ_ρ|} comes from |Im γ_ρ| < 1/2. Sharp cutoff φ = 1 fails (Remark 4.3): |φ̂(r−iy)| ≍ X^{|y|/2}/|r| gives a divergent tail; a fixed-width C³ ramp is the minimal repair, costing O(1/L). Any D₀ ∈ [T^{λ/4+ε}, T^{1−ε}] works.

key_items.statement: tr G̃ = aL·N(T,2T) + O(L√X); tr G̃² = 2πbL∫µ² + (T/π)Σ_{n≤X}Λ(n)²n⁻¹g(log n) + O(L·l·log l·(l²+X)) = (TL/2π)(ℓ₁² + L²/3)(1+O(E_T)), g = φ²⋆φ², E_T = w/L + (l²+X)log l/(Tl) + T^{λ/2−1}; hence ‖Ĝ‖²_F = (1/λ₁ + λ₁/3)N(1+O(E_T)) and (tr Ĝ)²/tr Ĝ² = F(λ₁)N. Errors: diagonal D = main; off-diagonal O1 ≪ L²X via Montgomery–Vaughan (Lemma 5.2, constant 3π/2, δ_n⁻¹ ≤ 2n); cross-terms µP_X ≪ l√X by one integration by parts against the cosine oscillation.

Stability (two integrations by parts, D = C − x²/2, E = ∫₀ˣD): v ≤ p₁ + |r(1)||D(1)| + |r′(1)||E(1)| + (sup_{[0,1]}|E|)·∫₀¹|r″|. Near-CUE laws (|N·S(j)−j| ≤ τ): sup|E| ≤ 1/(6N²) + τ/(2N).

key_items.name: The N = 256 extremal law and numeric ceiling
key_items.statement: 256-periodic law of marked configurations (exact rational weights w_c ≥ 0, Σw_c = 1; rational positions; marks m ∈ {1,2}, Σm = 256; from an exact-rational LP), grid form factor S(j) = Σ_c w_c|Σ_i m_{c,i}e^{2πij x_{c,i}/256}|²/256 satisfying |256S(j) − j| ≤ 3·10⁻⁴⁰ (0<j<256), |D(1)| ≤ 0.82395317, simple-point fraction p₀ = 10909258999421303588095230195816054408197/16·10³⁹ = 0.68182868746… exactly. Ceiling: v ≤ p₀ + 0.82395317|r(1)| + 2.5431316·10⁻⁶(|r′(1)| + ∫₀¹|r″|); with r(1)=0: every bandwidth-one config-by-config certificate certifies ≤ 0.6818287 + 2.55·10⁻⁶(...). Theorem B's 2/3 is within 0.01516 of this ceiling. Sole hypothesis: EnclOK (interval-arithmetic enclosures, sha256 cc3de991…, external to Lean); all else kernel-checked by decide.

key_items.name: Support-extension price list (Remark 1.1)
key_items.statement: Reaching simple-on-line proportions 0.70, 0.80, 0.90 by this route requires pair-correlation information on Fourier supports out to ≈ 1.04, 1.26, 1.70 respectively — beyond what is known unconditionally (or even under RH).

key_items.name: Higher moments (§7.5 d-f)
key_items.statement: Unconditional tr Ĝ^k available exactly in Rudnick–Sarnak range kλ < 2, so for λ ∈ (1/2,1) only k = 3 (λ < 2/3), and an odd moment does not lower the Christoffel function Λ₁(0): higher moments add NOTHING unconditionally. Sharp n₊ bound from 2m moments is 1 − Λ_m(0) (Chebyshev–Markov–Stieltjes). Conditionally: sine-kernel moments m_k(1) = 1, 4/3, 2, 13/4 (k ≤ 4); HL*(4,λ<1) [= Hardy–Littlewood-type additive correlations of Λ] ⇒ N₀ˢ/N ≥ 13/18 = 0.7222; HL*(all k) ⇒ proportion 1; 'RH itself is out of reach of the mechanism'.

key_items.name: RH-conditional distinct-zero improvement (§7.5 g)
key_items.statement: Under RH the third trace (triple correlation, Hejhal/Rudnick–Sarnak) permits cubic weights ψ(m) = m/2 + (2m²−m³)/18 + (4/9)1_{m=1}: N_d/N ≥ 1/2 + (2m₂−m₃)/18 + (4/9)(19/27) = 0.85082… with window v(s) = cos(8s/5) (2m₂−m₃ = 0.68524…), LP-optimal within span{m, m², m³, 1_{m=1}}; cf. 0.8477 [CGdL20].

key_items.name: Degree constraint (Remark 7.2)
key_items.statement: For degree m_F with Λ = bandwidth in mean-spacing units, formal outcome c = Λ/(1 + m_F Λ²/3) with Λ < Λ* = lim log T/log(conductor) (= 1/m in t-aspect); non-vacuous only if Λ* > 1/2 — a degree-one method. Individual GL(2): c = 6/13 < 1/2 ⇒ nothing, for any window. Family averaging (χ mod q, q → ∞) restores Λ* = 1 via orthogonality; sketch requires a Gevrey-class taper in Prop 4.2 (not carried out).

key_items.name: Theorem E and ξ′ variant
key_items.statement: Theorem E: all of A-D for any fixed primitive χ mod q > 1 (ν_{X,χ} = µ_χ + P_{X,χ}, no pole term; same 2/3, 5/6, 0.6725, 0.83625). ξ′ (Zeta23/XiPrime/): unconditionally ≥ 0.85838 of ξ′-zeros in (T,2T] simple on the line, ≥ 0.92919 distinct (flat window); 0.86864/0.93432 with quartic window v(s) = 1 − (7/100)(2s)² − (51/200)(2s)⁴; all zeros of ξ′ in open critical strip; Re ξ′/ξ > 0 on Re s ≥ 1. De-conditionalizes Farmer–Gonek–Lee's RH-conditional 0.8584.

key_items.name: Sharpness/extremal configuration (§7.5 b)
key_items.statement: Given only (tr, ‖·‖²_F, block structure, tr P₁ ≤ s₁), Prop 4.4 is sharp in all three parts: (2/3)N orthonormal simple on-line zeros + (1/6)N on-line doubles realize tr = N, ‖·‖²_F = (4/3)N, s₁ = (2/3)N, N_d = (5/6)N — the same extremal configuration as Montgomery's RH argument; replacing doubles by off-line pairs of depth → 0 is spectrally identical.

result.bandwidth_role: The bandwidth L = λ·log(T/2π), λ ≤ 1, is the support of the window φ (supp φ = [−L/2, L/2]), and it enters at four distinct load-bearing points. (1) Explicit-formula gate: W(f_k, f_l) uses the test k = f_k ∗ g̃_l with support ⊆ [−L, L], so ONLY prime powers n ≤ X = e^L = (T/2π)^λ appear on the prime side; "bandwidth one" (λ = 1) = Dirichlet polynomials of length T = pair-correlation test functions with Fourier support in [−1,1] in Montgomery's normalization. (2) The binding constraint λ ≤ 1 is Proposition 5.6's off-diagonal treatment: the second moment tr G̃² contains Σ_{n≠m} a_n a_m·(oscillating)/(log n − log m), which is NOT evaluated but only BOUNDED by the Montgomery–Vaughan generalized Hilbert inequality (Lemma 5.2, constant 3π/2, spacing δ_n⁻¹ ≤ 2n), giving |O1| ≪ L²X; the diagonal main term is TL³/6π, so the bound is admissible iff X ≪ TL, i.e. λ ≤ 1. For X ≫ T·log T the off-diagonal terms dominate and their EVALUATION would require Hardy–Littlewood prime-pair asymptotics Σ_m Λ(m)Λ(m+h) — equivalently Montgomery's pair-correlation conjecture for |α| > 1 (paper §7.5(a)). So it is a diagonal-only evaluation with MV absorbing the off-diagonal into the error; the arithmetic information beyond the diagonal is thrown away. (3) Dimension cap: the Gabor family at critical density has d = ⌊LT/2π⌋ = λ₁N members, so every rank/positive-index certificate is ≤ λ₁N (Prop 7.4): the method certifies nothing for λ ≤ 1/2 and its a priori ceiling is 100% only at λ = 1; combined with ‖Â‖²_F ≥ (tr Â)²/d the two-moment certificate is ≤ (2 − 1/λ₁)N. (4) Higher moments tr G̃^k are unconditionally available only in the Rudnick–Sarnak range kλ < 2, so at the operating point λ ≈ 1 only k = 1, 2 exist — precisely the two moments the rank–trace certificate consumes. The tail estimate (Prop 4.2) also carries a bandwidth factor X^{1/2} = T^{λ/2} (from e^{L|Im γ_ρ|}, |Im γ_ρ| < 1/2), harmless for λ ≤ 1 but fatal past λ = 2. Finally the PairCeiling development makes "bandwidth-one data" a formal notion: certificates (c₀, r) reading only the form-factor measure on [0,1] plus mean density plus integrality — and proves the 0.6818287 ceiling for ALL of them, so the 2/3 ↔ 0.6725 ↔ 0.6818 gap is intrinsic to bandwidth ≤ 1, not to the linear algebra.
limitations: No bearing on RH in either direction (paper §1.5): the certificate is a lower bound only; the inputs (functional equation, explicit formula, mean values of length-≤T Dirichlet polynomials) are insensitive to o(N) off-line zeros and are satisfied by Davenport–Heilbronn functions and Epstein zeta functions of class number > 1 for which RH-analogues are FALSE. Any route to RH itself must use an input that these counterexamples violate (Euler product/multiplicativity beyond L²-means).

λ ≤ 1 is essential and provably expensive to pass: for X ≫ T log T the off-diagonal prime sums require Hardy–Littlewood-strength prime-pair information (≡ pair-correlation conjecture for α > 1). The method certifies nothing at all for λ ≤ 1/2 (Prop 7.4 cap: certificate ≤ (2−1/λ₁)N ≤ 0).

The rank–trace certificate is provably tight (Lean TightMult.lemmaR_tight): given only tr, ‖·‖²_F, the block structure, and n₊, an on-line double zero and an off-line pair at depth → 0 are indistinguishable (both charge 4), so 'two thirds' cannot be pushed to 'all' by better linear algebra on the same two moments; the extremal configuration ((2/3)N orthonormal simples + (1/6)N doubles/deep pairs) realizes all constraints.

Bandwidth-one ceiling (Lean PairCeiling, hypothesis EnclOK only): NO certificate (c₀, r) of the Theorem-B type, valid configuration-by-configuration against bandwidth-one data, certifies simple-zero proportion > 0.6818287 + 2.55·10⁻⁶(|r′(1)| + ∫|r″|) (r(1) = 0). So even the optimal-window 0.6725 is within 0.0094 of a hard wall; 0.70/0.80/0.90 need Fourier support ≈ 1.04/1.26/1.70.

Higher unconditional moments are useless: available only for kλ < 2 (Rudnick–Sarnak), and for λ ∈ (1/2, 1) the only accessible extra moment (k = 3, λ < 2/3) does not improve the Christoffel-function bound; for λ ≤ 1/2 many moments exist but the dimension cap voids them. Even granting ALL moments (full Hardy–Littlewood, HL*(k₀, λ) for all k₀): proportion → 1 of simple zeros on the line, but 'RH itself is out of reach of the mechanism' — o(N) exceptional zeros remain invisible.

Degree-one method: for an individual L-function of degree m the usable bandwidth is Λ < 1/m and the certificate 2 − 1/c with c = Λ/(1+Λ²/3) is vacuous for m ≥ 2 (GL(2): c = 6/13 < 1/2, nothing for any window).

Slow convergence / no finite-T content: the certified ratio approaches its limit like 1 − O(1/L) = 1 − O(1/log T); numerically at all accessible heights (T ≤ 10⁶) the flat-window certificate is ≈ +0.40 to +0.42, well below 2/3·N — Theorems A–E are strictly T → ∞ statements; also the constants c(λ) are effective but the log log T/log T loss at λ = 1 is intrinsic to the endpoint.

Orthonormalisation is blocked: the Gram matrix M of the Gabor family has ≍ (w/L)d tiny eigenvalues; controlling W on those directions would need bounds on P_X over windows of length 1/L, i.e. Lindelöf-type information — the argument deliberately works in non-orthonormal coordinates where only inertia (coordinate-free) survives.

The zero-side second moment cannot be read termwise: a pair at depth |β−1/2| contributes ≍ X^{|2β−1|} to ‖Â‖²_F, so no unconditional termwise bound exists — forcing the prime-side detour and the loss of all off-diagonal zero-pair information.
extension_hooks: Off-diagonal prime sums: Prop 5.6 BOUNDS Σ_{n≠m} a_n a_m(...)/(y_n − y_m) by Montgomery–Vaughan instead of evaluating it. Any partial evaluation (e.g. averaged Hardy–Littlewood for Λ-correlations, known on average à la Montgomery–Soundararajan/Goldston) feeding a two-moment certificate at effective λ slightly > 1 would break the 0.6818 ceiling; the paper quantifies the payoff curve (support 1.04 → 0.70).

The moment→count machinery is already laid out (§7.5 d-f): n₊ ≥ (1 − Λ_m(0))d via Christoffel functions of the moment sequence d⁻¹tr(G̃/ℓ₁)^k. Proving HL*(4, λ) (fourth moment = sine-kernel value 13/4, encoding Σ(Λ∗Λ)(m)(Λ∗Λ)(m+h) asymptotics for |h| ≤ X²/T) yields 13/18 ≈ 0.7222 unconditionally. This is the sharpest concrete conjecture-to-constant hook in the artifact.

Family averaging (Remark 7.2(iii)): Lemma 3.2 is linear in tr and ‖·‖²_F, so both commute with averaging over families; orthogonality of characters restores bandwidth Λ* = 1 for q-averaged Dirichlet families, promising 2/3 of zeros on the line on average over χ mod q with T as small as a power of log q. Missing ingredient is explicitly named: a Gevrey-class taper making the Prop 4.2 tail work at tiny T. Concrete, unstarted project.

Under RH the third trace is a theorem (triple correlation) and the cubic-weight LP gives N_d ≥ 0.85082; the same LP framework (weights in span{m, m², m³, 1_{m=1}}, Schur–Horn majorisation constraint) generalizes to any new trace input — a template for converting each new correlation theorem into a zero-count.

The ceiling theorem itself is an extension target: it covers certificates valid CONFIGURATION-BY-CONFIGURATION against bandwidth-one data. Certificates exploiting positivity constraints that the 256-periodic law violates but true zeta satisfies (e.g. F(α) ≥ 0 for |α| > 1 — used by Chirre–Gonçalves–de Laat under RH to reach 0.6792 — or lower bounds on F beyond [−1,1], or non-configurationwise/average validity) are explicitly OUTSIDE the ceiling's scope. Making any F(α)-positivity for |α| > 1 unconditional (for the complex-zero form factor of [BGSTB24]) would immediately re-open the SDP route.

Window optimization for ξ′ (and ξ^(j)): the quartic window 1 − (7/100)(2s)² − (51/200)(2s)⁴ is an ad hoc polynomial, not the solution of the ξ′-analogue of the variational problem (7.3); solving the corresponding Euler–Lagrange equation should push 0.86864 toward (but below) the RH-conditional 0.8825, and combining with Wu's 0.86957 on-line count is a nontrivial merge.

Sylvester/inertia beyond two moments: Prop 4.5's inequalities (s₁ ≥ 2n₊^θ(G̃) − N, N_d ≥ n₊^θ(G̃)) are configuration-free — they hold for ANY 1−ρ̄-symmetric locally finite multiset with log-density. Any new spectral lower bound on n₊ of a structured Hermitian matrix (operator-norm information, eigenvalue rigidity, band-matrix theory for the specific kernel Φ(τ_k − τ_l)-against-ν_X) plugs in directly without touching the arithmetic.

The Lean LinAlg core (von Neumann trace inequality, both directions of Sylvester inertia, rank–trace, Weyl — namespace RHLinalg, contributed to the ecosystem) plus the abstract SeamMult/Assembly layers are engineered so that a new zero-side inequality or a new prime-side asymptotic can be swapped in; the k_c-form of Lemma R (rank_trace_mult_k) is stated leak-free for arbitrary real weights m_j‖v_j‖², i.e. already accommodates non-integer 'effective multiplicities' from imperfect sampling — a hook for windows beyond critical density or multi-scale families.

Hybrid q-T uniformity (Remark 7.2(i)): H(1/(1+ϑ)) for q ≤ T^ϑ, positive for ϑ < √6/3 ≈ 0.816 — stated as unchecked; carrying out the uniform error terms would give the first unconditional positive-proportion critical-line result uniform in conductor by this method.

The 256-periodic extremal law itself (exact-rational LP over marked point configurations with marks in {1,2}) is a new combinatorial object: the LP dual certificates characterize exactly which linear functionals of bandwidth-one data are saturated; studying its structure (why p₀ = 0.68182868746, why near-CUE rows) may reveal which additional constraint (three-point positivity? Fourier-positivity of higher correlations?) is cheapest to add to move the ceiling.
